tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: ShareOnboardingGuide
tools.description:
Upload the ONBOARDING.md in the current directory and return a share link teammates can open in Claude Code. Call this after the user has confirmed the final content.

When called with the default mode='check': if a local ONBOARDING.md is present, uploads it to the most-recently-updated org guide (or creates one if none exist) and returns a fresh link. If no local file is present, returns the existing link without uploading (status: has_existing).

'update': upload to a specific guide by short_code. 'create': always make a new link. 'delete': remove a guide.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_resize
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab to test responsive layouts. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).
    spaces_filter: Comma-separated list of space keys to filter by.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of simplified Confluence page objects.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue
entries.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue including its Epic links and relationship information.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.
    fields: Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'), a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'), '*all' for all fields, or omitted for essentials.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    comment_limit: Maximum number of comments.
    properties: Issue properties to return.
    update_history: Whether to update issue view history.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira issue object.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue_dates
entries.description:
Get date information and status transition history for a Jira issue.

Returns dates (created, updated, due date, resolution date) and optionally
status change history with time tracking for workflow analysis.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: The Jira issue key.
    include_status_changes: Whether to include status change history.
    include_status_summary: Whether to include aggregated time per status.

Returns:
    JSON string with issue dates and optional status tracking data.

include_status_changes.description: Include status change history with timestamps and durations

include_status_summary.description: Include aggregated time spent in each status

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search
entries.description:
Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    jql: JQL query string.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return.
    limit: Maximum number of results.
    start_at: Starting index for pagination.
    projects_filter: Comma-separated list of project keys to filter by.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    page_token: Pagination token from a previous search result (Cloud only).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the search results including pagination info.

jql.description:
JQL query string (Jira Query Language). Examples:
- Find Epics: "issuetype = Epic AND project = PROJ"
- Find issues in Epic: "parent = PROJ-123"
- Find by status: "status = 'In Progress' AND project = PROJ"
- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"
- Find recently updated: "updated >= -7d AND project = PROJ"
- Find by label: "labels = frontend AND project = PROJ"
- Find by priority: "priority = High AND project = PROJ"

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

projects_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of project keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER if provided.

page_token.description: (Optional) Pagination token from a previous search result. Cloud only — Server/DC uses start_at for pagination.

You are auditing FED (front-end dev) effort estimates for the Zimmermann SFCC PWA Kit project. Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa

## House context you MUST factor into every estimate

- Stack: Salesforce PWA Kit v3 on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10, React + Chakra UI, TypeScript-only inside `overrides/`.
- **Overrides pattern is a real cost multiplier.** To change any base SFCC component you must first copy it from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` into the mirrored path under `overrides/`, convert JS→TS, fix imports, verify it renders. That "copy-first" step alone is typically 0.25–1 day per non-trivial file before any functional change. Check whether the override already exists in `overrides/` — if it does, that cost is already paid; if not, it isn't.
- **8 storefronts / 11 locales** (AU, US domestic, US intl, UK, EU domestic, EU intl, HK, ME). Anything site-conditional multiplies build + verification effort.
- Every new component needs a `.stories.tsx`; logic-heavy code needs a `.test.ts(x)`. That is mandatory per project rules, so it is inside the FED estimate, not outside it.

## 1. The current max-quantity cap — the prior investigation is PARTIALLY WRONG

There are **two independent caps**, not one, and only the PDP one is purely hardcoded.

### A. PDP cap — HARDCODED. Claim CONFIRMED for the PDP.

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`

```
148: /** Frontend-enforced limit (SFCC-196). SFCC has no platform max-order-quantity field. */

```

Consumed at exactly one place, line 1330-1331:
```
1330:                  maxOrderQuantity={MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY}
1331:                  basketProductItems={basket?.productItems ?? []}
```

Module-scope `const`, no export, no config, no Salesforce read. This is the only cap on the PDP.

### B. Cart cap — already Salesforce-backed (with a hardcoded fallback). Claim REFUTED for the cart.

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`

```
38: const DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY = 3;
...
51: export const getMaxOrderQuantity = (product: ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity): number => {
52:   const value = product?.c_maxOrderQuantity;
53:   return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0 ? value : DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY;
54: };
```

This is materially important to your estimate. The file's own docblock (lines 3-36) documents that:
- `c_maxOrderQuantity` is a **Zimmermann-custom SFCC attribute** — a real BM site preference (Integer, default 3, min 1, per-site) surfaced onto SCAPI via a `dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET` hook, per Confluence `TSD-SFCC-268` (page id 406913046).
- As of that commit, TSD-SFCC-268 was **still v0.1 Draft, Technical Lead sign-off Pending**, and a live dev-sandbox probe found **no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product — the afterGET hook is not deployed**.
- The TSD's stated resolution order is: **product override (SFCC-703) → site preference → hardcoded value**. Note: that resolution order is per-product/per-site — **customer group is not in it.**
- Lines 31-36 explicitly state the duplication is deliberate: `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` is independent of the PDP's `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` rather than shared, because a shared constant "would need reworking the day the real per-site preference ships anyway."

Consumers of `getMaxOrderQuantity` (all cart-side, none on PDP):
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-item/index.tsx:168` (import), `:363` — `max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useCartMergeAndCap.ts:4`, `:43-44`

## 2. Base SFCC comparison

Base has **no max-order-quantity concept for ordinary products at all**.

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view/index.jsx`
  - `:161` — `maxOrderQuantity = null` (prop default: **no cap**)
  - `:769` — `{...(maxOrderQuantity != null && {max: maxOrderQuantity})}`
  - `:1047` — `maxOrderQuantity: PropTypes.number`
- The **only** base caller that ever passes it is the bonus-product flow: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx:398` — `const maxOrderQuantity = Math.max(0, finalMaxBonusItems - finalSelectedBonusItems)`, passed at `:474`. That is a bonus-item allowance, not a purchase cap.
- Base PDP `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx` renders `ProductView` at lines 675, 707, 789 and **never passes `maxOrderQuantity`**.

What base *does* read off the product — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-derived-product.js`:
```
37:    const stockLevel = product?.inventory?.stockLevel || 0
38:    const stepQuantity = product?.stepQuantity || 1
39:    const minOrderQuantity = stockLevel > 0 ? product?.minOrderQuantity || 1 : 0
40:    const initialQuantity = product?.quantity || product?.minOrderQuantity || 1
```
So base reads `inventory.stockLevel`, `stepQuantity`, `minOrderQuantity` — all real SCAPI product fields — but there is **no `maxOrderQuantity` field on the SCAPI product**, which is exactly why Zimmermann invented `c_maxOrderQuantity`. Base enforcement is orderability/stock only, via `validateOrderability(variant, product, quantity, stockLevel)` at `product-view/index.jsx:138-150`.

## 3. Where quantity is enforced on the PDP

**Important structural fact:** the PDP does not show a quantity picker. `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1332` — `showQuantityPicker={false}`. So the PDP cap is not a stepper `max`; it is a **basket-aggregate gate on the Add to Bag button**.

Owner of the logic: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`

The gate, lines 589-597:
```
589:    const isMaxOrderQtyReached = useMemo(() => {
590:      if (maxOrderQuantity == null) return false;
591:      const productId = variant?.productId;
592:      if (!productId) return false;
593:      const inBag = basketProductItems
594:        .filter((item) => item.productId === productId)
595:        .reduce((sum, item) => sum + (item.quantity ?? 0), 0);
596:      return inBag >= maxOrderQuantity;
597:    }, [maxOrderQuantity, basketProductItems, variant]);
```
Note it keys on **`variant.productId`**, i.e. the size-level SKU — already per-SKU, which helps the estimate.

## 2. Template build/install pipeline

Two scripts, one Contentful **Environment Template** named `'Zimmermann Content Model'` (the literal must match in both files).

**`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js`**
Reads every `.js` in `content-types/` (`fs.readdirSync().filter(f => f.endsWith('.js')).sort()`), maps each to a `contentTypeTemplate` + optional `editorInterfaceTemplate`, then get-or-creates the org-scoped template by **name** under `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID` and bumps its version. Touches no space or environment. Requires `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` + `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`.

**`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs`**
Validates then installs the template's current version into `--target <envId>`, polling `environmentTemplateInstallation` until terminal status (120s timeout). Refuses to install on any unresolved validation finding unless `--force`. Supports `--dry-run`, `--takeover <ids>` (adopt pre-existing unmanaged content types), `--delete-deleted-fields`.

Per `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/contentful/README.md`:

2. `npm run sync:contentful` — builds/updates the org template.
3. `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` — **once per environment**.

**Files that change for SFCC-173:** one new `scripts/contentful/content-types/faq.js` (+ likely `faqItem.js`), and optionally `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts` (`CONTENT_TYPE_IDS`) and `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts` (TS types).

## 6. CSP — and the real answer on JSON-LD

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts`, 275 lines. `useDefaults: true` (`:116`). `script-src` is at `:131-151` — an allowlist of third-party hosts only (Google Maps/Places, Adyen, Stripe, PayPal, Apple Pay, Measmerize, Klarna, `storage.googleapis.com`, `*.demandware.net`).

Note also the two-layer merge: `overrides/app/ssr.js:129` applies `defaultPwaKitSecurityHeaders` **before** `helmet()` at `:131-135`. The runtime middleware patches `res.setHeader` and unions its required directives into whatever helmet emits (`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/middleware/security.js:40` — `'script-src': ["'self'", "'unsafe-eval'", runtimeAdmin, siteDotCom]`; union at `:107`). Final effective `script-src` ≈ the app allowlist ∪ `'self' 'unsafe-eval'` + MRT admin + site.com. Still no `'unsafe-inline'`, still no nonce.

**(b) This does not block JSON-LD.** `<script type="application/ld+json">` is a *data block*, not an executable script — the HTML spec's "prepare the script element" algorithm never classifies it as classic/module, so it is never executed and the CSP inline-script check is never invoked. Emitting JSON-LD requires **no CSP change**. I want to be precise rather than reassuring here, so three caveats for the estimate:

1. **Do not attach a nonce to the JSON-LD tag "to be safe."** Under CSP3, introducing any nonce or hash into `script-src` disables `'unsafe-inline'` for the whole directive. This file already documents that exact footgun biting them twice in `style-src-elem` (`:37-41` and `:200-209`, the latter noting a live 2026-09-07 breakage). Adding a nonce to `script-src` risks the same class of regression against `'unsafe-eval'`/third-party payment scripts.
2. **React-helmet + JSON-LD content must go through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`** or a single string child. Passing an object or interpolated fragments to a `<script>` child under helmet is a known source of silent empty output — budget a little time to verify the SSR'd bytes, not just the React tree.
3. **`script-src-attr` is `'none'`** (helmet default, not overridden) — irrelevant to JSON-LD, but means no inline event handlers if any vendor snippet is ever inlined.

<result># Social Login at Checkout — Evidence Report

## Headline

Zimmermann has **already built and shipped a complete, Figma-branded Apple + Google sign-in stack** (SFCC-742 / SFCC-926 / SFCC-11) — hooks, buttons, icons, theme recipe, tests, stories — and social login is **enabled in config on every tier today**. It is wired into the **wishlist** auth drawer only. It is **not** wired into checkout, and checkout currently falls back to the **base SFCC unstyled** social buttons.

I also found one likely-live defect: the **IDP redirect-back route `/social-callback` appears never to be registered** (chip raised separately).

---

## 1. Base SFCC social login support

### Component inventory (only two files exist)
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/social-login/index.jsx`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/social-login/index.test.jsx` (39 lines)

There is no `social-login/**` subtree beyond these. `app/components/social-icons/` is unrelated — it is the footer's Facebook/Instagram/Twitter/YouTube **marketing** links, not auth.

### Supported IDPs — exactly two
`social-login/index.jsx:26-41` defines `IDP_CONFIG` with exactly **`apple`** and **`google`**. No Facebook, no others. Matching is case-insensitive (`index.jsx:57-60`, `name.toLowerCase()`), and an unknown IDP is logged as an error and filtered out of render (`index.jsx:62-72`, `:93-94`).

Icons ship OOTB: `index.jsx:19` imports `{AppleIcon, GoogleIcon}`, defined at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons/index.jsx:147` and `:172` from `app/assets/svg/apple.svg` and `app/assets/svg/google.svg`.

Button labels are bare — `'Apple'` / `'Google'` (`index.jsx:31, :38`), **not** "Sign in with Apple". Styling is generic Chakra: `variant="outline"`, `borderColor="gray.500"`, `color="blue.600"` (`index.jsx:106-109`).

### Auth mechanism (two-legged OAuth redirect)
**Leg 1 — outbound** (`social-login/index.jsx:50, :74-88`):
```js
const authorizeIDP = useAuthHelper(AuthHelpers.AuthorizeIDP)
setSessionJSONItem('returnToPage', window.location.pathname)
await authorizeIDP.mutateAsync({hint: name, redirectURI})
```
`redirectURI` = `buildRedirectURI(useAppOrigin(), getConfig()?.app?.login?.social?.redirectURI)` (`index.jsx:53-55`).

**Leg 2 — return** (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/social-login-redirect/index.jsx`):
- `:42` `useAuthHelper(AuthHelpers.LoginIDPUser)`
- `:54-71` on mount, reads `searchParams.code`, calls `loginIDPUser.mutateAsync({code, redirectURI, usid?})`
- `:74-94` once `customer.isRegistered`, clears `returnToPage`, calls `mergeBasket` with `createDestinationBasket: true`, then navigates back to `returnToPage` or `/account`

SDK surface confirmed in `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/useAuthHelper.d.ts:11,13` (`AuthorizeIDP: "authorizeIDP"`, `LoginIDPUser: "loginIDPUser"`) and `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/auth/index.d.ts:36,41,446-458`.

### Routes
`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes.jsx`:
- `:41` `const SocialLoginRedirect = loadable(() => import('./pages/social-login-redirect'))`
- `:56` `export const routes = [...]` — the **static** array. Contains no social route.

all using the identical pattern `const {social = {}} = getConfig().app.login || {}` → `isSocialEnabled: !!social?.enabled`, `idps: social?.idps`.

The chain is fully wired OOTB:

rendered under a divider + `"Or Login With"` heading (`login-state.jsx:28-33`), alongside a "Secure Link" (passwordless) and "Password" button.

```ts
onSignInWithGoogle?: () => void
```

## 5. Config keys — and their current values

## 6. Blocking defect found

`/social-callback` **appears not to be registered as a route.**

`overrides/app/routes.tsx:15` imports only the **static named export**:
```ts
import { routes as _routes } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes';
```
and spreads it at `:88`, then calls `configureRoutes` on its own array at `:114-117`. The base **default export** (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes.jsx:131`), which is the only place the social route is appended (`:153-157`), is **never invoked**.

- `.claude/registry/routes.md` (generated 2026-09-23 from `overrides/app/routes.tsx`) lists **no** `/social-callback`, `/passwordless-login-landing` or `/reset-password-landing`

**Repo state at audit:** branch `feature/SFCC-11_cart`, with unresolved merge conflicts (`UU`) in `.claude/registry/*` and a few `ui-kits` files. `overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/payment.tsx` is `M` (staged modified); `checkout-header.tsx` is untracked (`??`).

**Apple Pay / Google Pay express checkout is ABSENT as a working flow.** What exists is: (a) two **non-functional, click-handler-less** wallet buttons in the cart drawer, and (b) an **inherited, config-disabled** Salesforce Payments express path from the base template that is wired into PDP but cannot activate because `sfPayments.enabled = false`.

Note line 379-381: the category from the **path** is injected into the refine array as `cgid=<id>` — i.e. the path segment is converted into a query-style refinement before hitting the API.

The actual parsing lives in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-search-params.js`:

```js
// use-search-params.js:23-33
export const useSearchParams = (searchParams = DEFAULT_SEARCH_PARAMS, parseRefine = true) => {
    const {search} = useLocation()
    const searchParamsObject = { ...searchParams, ...parse(search.substring(1), parseRefine) }
    return [searchParamsObject, {stringify, parse}]
}
```
```js
// use-search-params.js:73-95
export const parse = (searchParamsStr, parseRefine = true) => {
    const params = queryString.parse(searchParamsStr, PARSE_OPTIONS)
    params.refine = Array.isArray(params.refine) ? params.refine : [params.refine].filter(Boolean)
    if (parseRefine) {
        params._refine = params.refine
        params.refine = params.refine.reduce((acc, curr) => ({
            ...acc,
            ...queryString.parse(curr, {...PARSE_OPTIONS, parseNumbers: false,
                arrayFormat: 'separator', arrayFormatSeparator: '|'})
        }), {})
    }
    return params
}
```

So the wire format is `?refine=c_refinementColor%3Dblack%7Cwhite&refine=c_size%3D8&sort=...&offset=...`. Multi-value within one facet is pipe-joined. `stringify` (use-search-params.js:42-63) is the inverse. `DEFAULT_SEARCH_PARAMS = {limit: 25, offset: 0, sort: 'best-matches', refine: []}` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js:18`).

```ts
const handleBufferedToggle = (
  value: { value: string | number },
  attributeId: string,
  selected: boolean,
  allowMultiple = true,
) => {
  const stringValue = String(value.value);
  if (!allowMultiple) {
```

### Is a full category tree available at build/SSR time to enumerate filter combinations?

**No, not as it stands.** Specifics:

- The only tree fetch is `_app/index.tsx:173` with **`levels: 1`** — one level below root. It is a **runtime** (SSR-prepass/client) React Query call, not a build-time artefact. `_app/index.tsx:176` flattens it: `const categories = flatten((categoriesTree || {}) as CategoryNode, 'categories');`
- Deeper levels are fetched **lazily per menu item** as the shopper hovers/expands.
- Nothing walks or persists the tree. There is **no** category manifest, JSON dump, prerender list, sitemap generator, or build script that enumerates categories. `scripts/` contains `generateRegistry.mjs` (a Claude-facing code registry, not routes-for-SEO), `crawlZimmermann.py`, and deploy/env tooling — **no sitemap script, no static route enumeration.**
- `ssr.js:221` is `app.get('*', runtime.render)` — no prerender list.

**However** — the *structure* is mechanically derivable without a tree walk, because of `categoryIdFromPathSegments` / `categoryUrlBuilder` (url.ts:143-192). Given any category id, its URL is computable and vice-versa. So enumeration needs one recursive `getCategory(levels=N)` crawl, which nothing currently performs.

content.text:
Second cluster verified. Both findings hold, and one of them isn't an estimate error at all.

## Didomi is not built — and it gates two of the sized items

Independently confirmed: `package.json` has **5 runtime dependencies** (2 Adyen, 3 Contentful) and no consent library. Zero `didomi` references anywhere in `overrides/`, `config/` or `worker/`. [config/sit.js:46](config/sit.js:46) says it in a code comment — *"Didomi isn't built"*. `projectState.md` lists Didomi, Emarsys, Inside Chat and Avalara all as **Not started**.

That matters because AGENTS.md's rule is absolute: no third-party script loads before Didomi consent, fail-closed. So:

| Ticket | Table FED | Bottom-up | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-857** Emarsys Web Extend | 3 | **6** | UNDER by 3 — and +5–8 more if it has to build Didomi first |
| **SFCC-858** Co-browsing | 3 | **4.5** best case | UNDER — realistically not estimable |
| **SFCC-946** Avalara expansion | 2 | **0.5–0.75** | MIS-ATTRIBUTED, over by ~1.5 |

SFCC-857's 3 days prices dropping in the Scarab tag. The actual bulk is per-page-type event mapping — identity, browse, cart-on-every-view, purchase, SPA route dispatch — about 2.75 days of it, all net-new because there is **no tracking abstraction at all** (no `dataLayer`, no `gtag`, nothing). SFCC-858 omits PII/payment masking and the consent-prompt UI entirely, and Inside Chat isn't even embedded yet — `INSIDE_CHAT_SITE_TOKEN` is blank in `.env.sample` and the integration doc never mentions co-browsing.

## SFCC-946 may not be chargeable scope at all

This one goes past the estimate. The front end renders `basket.taxTotal` straight from the SCAPI payload — I confirmed `order-summary` is **not overridden** and base [index.jsx:252](node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/order-summary/index.jsx:252) renders the field directly. The output is byte-identical whether Avalara or SFCC native tables computed it. Real FE tax work is already ticketed under SFCC-462 and SFCC-43, so 2 FED days here double-books it.

But the bigger problem is the baseline. Three docs give three different answers about which markets Avalara already covers:

- **PRC-07** — [pricing-currency-globale.md:28](.docs/prd/pricing-currency-globale.md:28), *confirmed, signed off Emma/Rebecca **24 June***: "Avalara covers **AU, EU, US, and UK** domestic storefronts for go-live."
- **architecture.md:245**, updated **19 June**: US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, **EU domestic**. "UK uses SFCC native VAT tables."
- **PAY-067** — [checkout.md:191](.docs/prd/checkout.md:191): Avalara for US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia only. "**All other domestic storefronts use SFCC native tax tables.**"

SFCC-946 is titled "Scope Expansion" and the note says "Expansion to EU, UK and Domestic markets". The most recent and most senior of those three statements — PRC-07, signed off by the business owners on 24 June — already puts EU and UK inside the go-live baseline. **If PRC-07 stands, SFCC-946 is expanding into scope that's already committed, and it shouldn't be consuming enhancement budget.**

That's a Doc-integrity call under AGENTS.md, not something to quietly pick a side on.

---

Five agents still running (checkout/auth, returns, SEO, PDP, cart/payments, plus the unestimated-rows sweep). I'll consolidate everything into one corrected table when they land.

**What you're missing on this pass:** SFCC-857 will build a browser-side event pipeline — identity, product view, cart state, purchase — that substantially duplicates the AAB-002 GTM dataLayer, and `sprintScope.md` puts analytics in Sprint 7. Building Emarsys' own queue first means paying for that plumbing twice and then reconciling two sources of truth for revenue numbers. That's a sequencing decision for you and Tell No Lies before either gets committed, not a number to correct. If you say nothing I'll flag it in the final report as a recommendation rather than act on it.

## 1. SFCC-866 — Auto-remove cart item when moving to wishlist if already in wishlist

- `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (817 lines) — membership test is a synchronous in-memory `.some()` over `wishlist.customerProductListItems`, short-circuiting before any network call. **No new fetch needed.**
- `overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts`, `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` (421 lines), `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/`

**FED work breakdown (drawer-only, after SFCC-272 lands):**

| Item | Days |
|---|---|

## 2. SFCC-804 — Marketing opt-in capture for Apple Pay / Google Pay express

**What it actually asks for:** capture marketing consent from shoppers using express wallets, who never see the opt-in checkbox.

**AC quality: NO — 0 ACs, and the ticket says so itself:** *"This story is currently a placeholder — no solution has been agreed... Requires input from Emma/Rebecca (business), Keira (UX), and Tim (technical feasibility) before ACs can be written."*

**What exists already:**

## SFCC-866 contradicts work being written on your current branch

`feature/SFCC-11_cart` is implementing SFCC-272 AC6, which specifies the **opposite** of what SFCC-866 asks for. This isn't inference — AC6 is cited in four places in live code:

SFCC-866 says remove it anyway. The membership check is already a synchronous in-memory `.some()` — no new API call needed — so the functional change is **one line moved**.

**Cost depends entirely on timing:** ~0.25 day folded into SFCC-272 before it ships, or **~1.5 days** later, spent almost entirely on re-opening, reversing and re-testing code being written this sprint. The table says 2 days. So the number is only mildly over — but the sequencing is worth more than the estimate.

## Two more items are sized against things the PRD says don't exist

**SFCC-804** (FED 2 days, marketing opt-in for Apple/Google Pay express). [checkout.md §17 Explicit Non-Goals](.docs/prd/checkout.md) — *"Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna (**August 2026**)"*. content.text:
Verified on `develop`. This one is the most serious thing the audit has turned up.

## SFCC-947 is dismissed on the tracker by pointing at the ticket that caused it

The row says *"Not an enhancement — Jasmijn has a ticket and is being built"* → SFCC-101. That's backwards. **SFCC-101 shipped the pattern SFCC-947 objects to, and it's on `develop` now.**

In `zimmSizeSelector/index.tsx` on `origin/develop`, "Find your size" renders **twice**, both calling the same `onFindYourSizeClick`:

- **line 167** — `triggerRowRight`, beside the trigger. This is the placement SFCC-947 *recommends keeping*.
- **lines 210–214** — again inside the dropdown panel, in a `<div>` that is a **sibling of `<ul role="listbox">`**, paired with a Size Guide link.

And SFCC-101's **AC9 mandates the second one**: *"when they open the size selector, then they can find the 'Find your size' CTA down in the size selector."* So the two tickets conflict at acceptance-criteria level. They are not duplicates, and SFCC-947 is not covered.

The a11y problem is concrete, not stylistic. The panel declares `role="listbox"` with `aria-labelledby` and drives selection through `focusedIndex`, so its keyboard model is arrow-keys-within-the-`ul`. The two links sit **outside** that `ul`, so they're either unreachable by keyboard while the panel is open, or Tab-reachable in a way that pulls focus out of the composite widget mid-selection. Either way a screen reader announces "Find your size" twice in one context with nothing to tell them apart. That's WCAG 2.2 AA — 2.1.1 and 4.1.2 — against the target AGENTS.md sets.

Remediation is **~2–3 FED days including a11y testing**, but it can't start until someone decides whether AC9 stands. Worth settling before SFCC-101 clears SIT rather than after.

---
name: project-max-order-quantity
description: SFCC has no max-order-quantity field at all; the 3-per-SKU cap is a hardcoded frontend constant, contradicting a Done "BM Config" card
metadata:
  type: project
---

Verified 2026-09-16 two ways.

`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s generated types contain `minOrderQuantity` and `stepQuantity` and
**no `maxOrderQuantity`**. A live probe of the dev sandbox (site `ZimmermannAU`, shortCode
`qmyt7hks`, SLAS private-client guest token) returned `inventory`, `minOrderQuantity`,
`stepQuantity` and 19 `c_*` custom attributes — **none** quantity-related, so custom-attribute
exposure works and the max simply isn't configured.

The real enforcement is `const MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY = 3` at
`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:123`, whose comment already says SFCC has no platform
field (SFCC-196). `product-view`'s `isMaxOrderQtyReached` sums basket line items filtered on
`productId` and compares with `>=`; `maxOrderQuantity == null` means unrestricted.

**Contradiction:** SFCC-268 "PDP – Maximum Purchase Quantity – **BM Config**" is marked Ready for
SIT (Done, Sprint 3, Victor Crisostomo), and SFCC-250's ACs all say "the **configured** maximum of
3". Nothing reachable from the Shopper API was configured.

Caveat: dev sandbox and two products only — a sit/uat custom attribute isn't strictly ruled out.

**Why:** any story that says "the configured maximum" will send someone hunting for a Business
Manager setting that does not exist.

**How to apply:** build against the constant, promote it out of the PDP page so other surfaces read
one value rather than re-typing `3`, and don't treat SFCC-268 as having delivered a readable
setting. Related: [[project-cart-bundle-decisions]], [[project-cart-merge-mechanics]].

Verified 2026-09-16, **re-verified and amended 2026-09-24**.

**There are now two independent mechanisms, not one.**

- **Cart — SFCC-backed read path exists.** `overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`'s
  `getMaxOrderQuantity()` reads `c_maxOrderQuantity` off the SCAPI product response and falls back
  to its own `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY = 3`. Consumed by `product-item/index.tsx`,
  `useCartMergeAndCap.ts` and `cartDrawerContainer.tsx`.
- **PDP — still hardcoded.** `const MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY = 3` at
  `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:149`, used once at `:1330`. Not wired to the util.

**The attribute is still not populated.** That util's own docblock records a live dev-sandbox probe
finding no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product — the `afterGET` hook is not deployed. So the read
path degrades to the hardcoded 3 today and picks up the real value the day the hook ships.
`TSD-SFCC-268` (Confluence 406913046) is still **v0.1 Draft, Technical Lead sign-off Pending**, with
unfilled `[Name]` placeholders, and its resolution order is product override → site preference →
hardcoded. **Customer group is not a tier in it at all** — which matters because SFCC-703 asks for
exactly that.

**Correction to this memory's earlier advice:** it previously said to promote the constant out of
the PDP into one shared value. That was considered and **deliberately rejected** — the util's
docblock explains a shared constant would need reworking the day the real per-site preference
ships, since the two sit at different tiers of the TSD's resolution order. Don't re-propose it.

**Three tickets, one mechanism (2026-09-24):** SFCC-703 (customer-group + SKU override),
SFCC-172 (cart SKU override, `CouldHave`), and SFCC-250 (cart enforcement, **In Progress**, whose
ACs hardcode "the configured maximum of 3"). Resolve the overlap before re-estimating any of them.

**Why:** any story saying "the configured maximum" sends someone hunting for a Business Manager
setting that does not exist yet, and the PDP/cart split means a fix in one place silently leaves
the other on 3.

**How to apply:** wire the PDP to `getMaxOrderQuantity(product)` (the `product` is already in scope
at `:1330`) rather than adding a third constant; don't treat SFCC-268 as having delivered a
readable setting; and don't assume customer-group resolution is a frontend concern until the TSD
is signed. Related: [[project-cart-bundle-decisions]], [[project-cart-merge-mechanics]],
[[project-sprint6-duplicate-stories]].

# SFCC-133 — Checkout: Reduce Login Friction via Email & OTP

**What it actually asks for:** shopper enters email at checkout, gets a 6-digit code emailed, types it into 6 boxes with a 5:00 countdown, RESEND link and "USE A DIFFERENT EMAIL" — inside the login *drawer*.

**AC quality: NO ACs on SFCC-133** (JQL-confirmed `customfield_10231` empty). Its description is a sizing note, not requirements. **SFCC-588 does have ACs** (JQL-confirmed non-empty) — content unreadable via MCP. SFCC-588 is still `In Refinement`.

Far more than the estimate implies:

- `config/default.js:91` — `mode: 'email'`. This is the **typed-code** SLAS path, not magic-link. Already correct.
- `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` (421 lines) — `authorizePasswordless` + `loginPasswordless` wired end-to-end, plus basket merge.
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx` + `.../zimmAuthDrawerContent/` — a **branded login drawer is live today**, with an email step already labelled "Send code" (`emailForm.tsx:29`).
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/otp-auth/index.jsx` (374 lines) — a working 6/8-box OTP UI with auto-advance, paste, auto-submit. Plus `hooks/use-otp-inputs.js`, `hooks/use-countdown.js`.
- `.../pages/checkout-one-click/partials/one-click-contact-info.jsx` — a complete reference for checkout+OTP wiring, including a single-flight duplicate-send guard.

---

## Bottom line

The individual numbers are mostly defensible. **The tracker as a whole is not.**

| | FED days |
|---|---|
| FED budget (the page's own model: 2 sprints × 1 FED) | **20.0** |
| Booked as consumed | 12.5 |
| **Remaining** | **7.5** |
| Sized on the tracker, as written | **49.0** — 2.5× the whole budget |
| Sized on the tracker, after this audit | **53–88** — 2.6× to 4.4× |

Approved-but-never-booked work alone (SFCC-135, 704, 724, 859, 946) is **17.5 days as written** against **7.5 remaining** — a **10-day hole** before any correction, and 15–28 days after.

Three things matter more than any single number:

1. **The capacity model treats four disciplines as interchangeable.** BA finishes with ~11 days spare while FED is 10 short. The work mix is FED-heavy and the model doesn't know it.
2. **18 of 18 audited tickets have no acceptance criteria.** `customfield_10231` is null on every one. Every figure on that page estimates a paragraph.
3. **Five rows aren't estimating problems at all** — they're duplicates, mis-attributions, or requests that reverse a signed-off requirement. Correcting their day-counts would miss the point.

---

## 1. Corrected estimates

"Table" uses the page's own convention of splitting `FED + BED: n` evenly. Low/high reflect genuinely undecided scope, not estimating confidence.

| Ticket | What it is | Table | Low | High | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC-133 | Checkout email + OTP login | 3 | 3.25 | 8.0 | Scope undecided — delta vs full build |
| SFCC-135 | Social login Apple/Google | 3.5 | 5.75 | 7.5 | **UNDER** — the even split is wrong here |
| SFCC-142 | Returns link, conditional | 2.5 | 2.75 | 3.9 | Number ~right; **rule not buildable yet** |
| SFCC-143 | Returns portal pre-populate | 2 | 2.05 | 2.8 | **ABOUT RIGHT** ✓ |
| SFCC-155 | VIP private marketing URL | 1 | 1.8 | 2.3 | UNDER — cart restriction unpriced |
| SFCC-173 | FAQ/Article schema | 3 | 5.5 | 8.5 | UNDER — Contentful isn't SSR-available |
| SFCC-174 | AI extraction fields | 3 | 0.5 | 1.0 | **OVER — duplicate of SFCC-572** |
| SFCC-703 | Max qty by customer group | 2 | 1.5 | 4.5 | Right by accident; owner undecided |
| SFCC-704 | EU Declaration of Conformity | 2 | 3.25 | 3.75 | UNDER — 5 sites, not 2 |
| SFCC-710 | Wishlist confirmation toast | 2 | 2.0 | 3.5 | **Reversal of SFCC-434, not a duplicate** |
| SFCC-724 | Indexable filter pages | 5 | 5.25 | 16.0 | **UNSIZEABLE** — URL shape undecided |
| SFCC-804 | Wallet marketing opt-in | 2 | 0.0 | 3.25 | **NOT ESTIMABLE** — placeholder story |
| SFCC-857 | Emarsys Web Extend | 3 | 6.0 | 6.0 | UNDER — no tracking layer exists |
| SFCC-858 | Live-chat co-browsing | 3 | 4.5 | 4.5 | UNDER — that's a floor, not a ceiling |
| SFCC-859 | Field validation / regex | 5 | 8.0 | 8.0 | UNDER — 6 form hooks need copy-first |
| SFCC-866 | Cart→wishlist auto-remove | 2 | 0.25 | 1.5 | OVER — cheapest folded into SFCC-272 now |
| SFCC-946 | Avalara scope expansion | 2 | 0.5 | 0.75 | **MIS-ATTRIBUTED** — payload-driven |
| SFCC-950 | VIP rewards via Global-E | 3 | 0.0 | 2.0 | **MIS-ATTRIBUTED** — vendor iframe |
| | **Total** | **49.0** | **52.9** | **87.8** | vs **7.5 remaining** |

---

## 2. Defects in the capacity tables themselves

- **SFCC-142 is recorded twice, differently.** Main table `FED+BED 5, QA 3`; capacity table `FED 3.5 + DEV 3.5 = 7, QA 2`. Two dev-days appear or vanish depending on which table you read. It's a scope disagreement — 2.5 is credible as "delta on an existing order page", 3.5 as "includes standing the page up". Nobody wrote down which was meant.
- **SFCC-155 consumes Phase 1 capacity for non-Phase-1 work.** Booked as FED 1 + DEV 1 while its own note says "Not for Phase 1". Tash is flagged to fix the table; it hasn't happened.
- **SFCC-173 is booked as 3 consumed FED days while its status is still TBC.**
- **The even-split convention is unreliable.** It was applied to SFCC-155 and SFCC-143 but *not* to SFCC-142. For SFCC-135 it's actively wrong — `projectState.md:163` records the BED half as "SFCC OOTB configuration only", i.e. provisioning, not build. Nearly all the remaining work is front-end.

---

## 3. The five rows that aren't estimate problems

**SFCC-946 (Avalara) may not be chargeable scope at all.** Three docs give three different answers on which markets Avalara already covers, and the most recent — **PRC-07, signed off by Emma/Rebecca on 24 June** — already puts **AU, EU, US and UK** in the go-live baseline. That is exactly what SFCC-946 proposes to "expand" into. Separately the FE work is near zero: `order-summary` isn't overridden and base renders `basket.taxTotal` straight from the payload, identically whichever engine computed it. Real FE tax work is already ticketed as SFCC-462 and SFCC-43.

**SFCC-950 reverses a signed-off requirement.** `checkout.md:221` PAY-039: *"HK, ME, EU International: Retail Rewards **cannot** be redeemed online."* `account.md:289` logs CRM-022 as Open, "not currently scoped". The deliverable also lives inside Global-E's own iframe, and the data handoff is server-side SendCart, already spec'd under PRC-16. The ticket's own note says there are no legacy gold VICs internationally — zero affected customers.

**SFCC-174 duplicates SFCC-572**, which sits in epic SFCC-22 with **7 real acceptance criteria**. More broadly there are **two parallel SEO backlogs**: SFCC-724 ≈ SFCC-563 + SFCC-577, and SFCC-563 carries the *same* `DMU-023` label. Sizing the Enhancements copies books the same days twice. Deciding that the Enhancements epic owns no SEO work would recover ~6 FED days — most of the gap.

**SFCC-156 is not a duplicate of SFCC-135.** Jira records the link as **`Blocks`**, not Duplicate, and the ticket ("Duplicate Account Prevention & Apple Hide My Email") is **High**, carries CRM-005/033/034, and has **7 ACs**, three of them front-end. Marking it N/A doesn't remove ~2–3 FED days; it pushes them silently into SFCC-135's 7.

**SFCC-710 is a reversal, not a duplicate.** The tracker asks Jasmijn to check for duplication. There is none — but `product-detail/index.tsx:590` says verbatim: *"SFCC-434 — toast-free add… **Jasmijn confirmed the PDP badge has no confirmation message**, only the icon state change."* SFCC-710 asks for that message back.

---

## 4. Two live defects found while auditing

Neither is an estimate issue. Both are in shipped or shipping code.

### 4a. `/social-callback` has no registered route — social sign-in cannot complete

`social.enabled: true` on **dev, test, sit, uat, staging and production** (`config/*.js`), and `redirectURI` defaults to `/social-callback`. `overrides/app/ssr.js:115` already allowlists `^/social-callback`, so the path was expected to resolve.

But it never gets registered. `overrides/app/routes.tsx:15` imports the **static named export** `{routes as _routes}` and spreads it at line 90. The social route is appended only inside the base **default export function** (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes.jsx:131-157`), which nothing calls — our own default export at `routes.tsx:114` runs `configureRoutes(routes, …)` on the static array.

A shopper returning from Apple or Google would fall through to the `/:segments+` catch-all, resolve `social-callback` as a category, and land on not-found. `loginIDPUser` never runs. The social buttons in the wishlist auth drawer are already built and shipped.

*Verified statically, not exercised in a running environment. Worth a 5-minute confirmation on a preview target before anyone acts on it.*

### 4b. SFCC-947 is a real a11y defect, dismissed by pointing at the ticket that caused it

The row says *"Not an enhancement — Jasmijn has a ticket and is being built"* → SFCC-101. It's the other way round: **SFCC-101 shipped the pattern SFCC-947 objects to, and it's on `develop`.**

In `zimmSizeSelector/index.tsx` on `origin/develop`, "Find your size" renders twice, both calling the same handler — at **line 167** (`triggerRowRight`, the placement SFCC-947 recommends keeping) and again at **lines 210–214**, inside the dropdown in a `<div>` that is a **sibling of `<ul role="listbox">`**. SFCC-101's **AC9 mandates the second one**, so the two tickets conflict at AC level.

The panel drives selection through `focusedIndex` within the `ul`, so the two links sit outside that keyboard model — either unreachable while the panel is open, or Tab-reachable in a way that pulls focus out of the composite widget mid-selection. A screen reader announces "Find your size" twice with nothing to distinguish them. WCAG 2.2 AA, 2.1.1 and 4.1.2.

~2–3 FED days to remediate, but the AC9 decision has to land first. Worth settling before SFCC-101 clears SIT.

---

## 5. Why the estimates skew low — the systematic bias

They price the *feature*, not this codebase's cost of change.

- **No `overrides/app/pages/account/` exists.** 6,300 LOC of base account pages untouched. SFCC-142, 143, 710 and part of 859 all land there, and none of them carries the copy-first conversion.
- **No `overrides/app/components/seo/`, and zero `ld+json` anywhere** in overrides *or* base. SFCC-173 and SFCC-174 build the first structured-data plumbing, not an extension of it.
- **Zero regex validation exists in the base form layer** — 29 `required:`, 7 `validate:`, 1 `maxLength`, and **no `pattern:`** across ~68 field definitions in 8 hooks, only one of which is overridden. SFCC-859 is greenfield across every customer-editable field.
- **Didomi is not built** — 5 runtime dependencies in `package.json`, none consent-related; `config/sit.js:46` says so in a comment. It gates SFCC-857 and SFCC-858, and it's unscheduled.
- **No tracking layer at all** — no `dataLayer`, no `gtag`. SFCC-857's 3 days price a script drop-in; the event mapping is all net-new.

One correction to a premise used widely in planning: `config/sites.overlay.js` defines **11 PWA site configs over 8 SFCC sites** (EU domestic is four single-locale PWA sites on one SFCC site). Each is pinned to one locale. For FED work the multiplier is **11**.

---

## 6. Decisions that need a human

Ranked by what they unlock, not by ticket order.

| # | Decision | Owner | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | FED is 10+ days short on approved work. What comes off? | Marcel + squad leads + Tash | The whole plan |
| 2 | Does the Enhancements epic own any SEO work, or does it point at SFCC-22? | Emma, Bianca | ~6 FED days |
| 3 | SFCC-947 vs SFCC-101 AC9 — a11y defect on `develop` | Jasmijn + UI designer + Marcel | Before SFCC-101 clears SIT |
| 4 | Avalara market baseline: PRC-07 vs PAY-067 vs architecture.md | Emma/Rebecca + PAY-067 owner | Whether SFCC-946 is chargeable |
| 5 | SFCC-724: clean path URLs or query-string? | Sparro / Tell No Lies via Emma | A ~10-day swing |
| 6 | SFCC-866 — fold into SFCC-272 now or reverse it later? | Tim / Squad A | 0.25 day vs 1.5 |
| 7 | SFCC-133 — whole OTP build, or checkout delta on SFCC-587/588? | Tash | A 5-day swing |
| 8 | SFCC-859 vs SFCC-675 — both High, overlapping scope, both costed | Tash | Double-count |
| 9 | Delivery completion date via MuleSoft — will it exist? | Integration lead | SFCC-142's primary rule |
| 10 | Does "Approved" mean approved-to-spend or approved-in-principle? | Tash | How to read the whole page |

Two hygiene items worth one sweep rather than eighteen edits:

- **`MustHave` has stopped meaning anything.** SFCC-160, 176, 177, 144, 156 and 135 all still carry it from the original ENH-register import, including three the page treats as N/A or descoped. The Jira dashboard the page cites as its source of truth is running off that label.
- **None of the 18 tickets is in any sprint.** `sprint is not EMPTY` returns zero rows for all of them.

---

## 7. What I could not verify

- **The Confluence page itself would not load through the connector** after the first read — repeated timeouts and dropped connections on page 385318913, which appears to be size-related (smaller pages fetched fine). Table figures are from my initial successful read (v17); I could not re-check them at the end, nor read the page comments.
- **Acceptance-criteria text** for SFCC-588 and SFCC-590 — presence/absence confirmed via a JQL `customfield_10231 IS NOT EMPTY` probe, but the field body would not serialise.
- **The SFCC-22 SEO epic overlap** (SFCC-562/563/572/577) is the agent's finding from a working Jira session; my own confirming query was refused by the connector.
- **The `/social-callback` defect is a static read.** Not exercised against a running environment.
- **Trello is not connected** and is outside anything this audit can see.

Nothing was written to Jira or Confluence. This is read-only throughout.

# FED Estimate Audit — 9.2 Enhancements

**Source:** Confluence [9.2 Enhancements](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/385318913) (v17)
**Audited:** 24 September 2026 · Marcel Navarro, FED Lead
**Method:** every row with a FED figure read against its Jira ticket, its acceptance criteria, the `.docs/` requirement set, and the codebase. Bottom-up rebuild of each estimate, not a sanity-check of the existing one.

---

## Bottom line

The individual numbers are mostly defensible. **The tracker as a whole is not.**

| | FED days |
|---|---|
| FED budget (the page's own model: 2 sprints × 1 FED) | **20.0** |
| Booked as consumed | 12.5 |
| **Remaining** | **7.5** |
| Sized on the tracker, as written | **49.0** — 2.5× the whole budget |
| Sized on the tracker, after this audit | **53–88** — 2.6× to 4.4× |

Approved-but-never-booked work alone (SFCC-135, 704, 724, 859, 946) is **17.5 days as written** against **7.5 remaining** — a **10-day hole** before any correction, and 15–28 days after.

Three things matter more than any single number:

1. **The capacity model treats four disciplines as interchangeable.** BA finishes with ~11 days spare while FED is 10 short. The work mix is FED-heavy and the model doesn't know it.
2. **18 of 18 audited tickets have no acceptance criteria.** `customfield_10231` is null on every one. Every figure on that page estimates a paragraph.
3. **Five rows aren't estimating problems at all** — they're duplicates, mis-attributions, or requests that reverse a signed-off requirement. Correcting their day-counts would miss the point.

---

## 1. Corrected estimates

"Table" uses the page's own convention of splitting `FED + BED: n` evenly. Low/high reflect genuinely undecided scope, not estimating confidence.

| Ticket | What it is | Table | Low | High | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC-133 | Checkout email + OTP login | 3 | 3.25 | 8.0 | Scope undecided — delta vs full build |
| SFCC-135 | Social login Apple/Google | 3.5 | 5.75 | 7.5 | **UNDER** — the even split is wrong here |
| SFCC-142 | Returns link, conditional | 2.5 | 2.75 | 3.9 | Number ~right; **rule not buildable yet** |
| SFCC-143 | Returns portal pre-populate | 2 | 2.05 | 2.8 | **ABOUT RIGHT** ✓ |
| SFCC-155 | VIP private marketing URL | 1 | 1.8 | 2.3 | UNDER — cart restriction unpriced |
| SFCC-173 | FAQ/Article schema | 3 | 5.5 | 8.5 | UNDER — Contentful isn't SSR-available |
| SFCC-174 | AI extraction fields | 3 | 0.5 | 1.0 | **OVER — duplicate of SFCC-572** |
| SFCC-703 | Max qty by customer group | 2 | 1.5 | 4.5 | Right by accident; owner undecided |
| SFCC-704 | EU Declaration of Conformity | 2 | 3.25 | 3.75 | UNDER — 5 sites, not 2 |
| SFCC-710 | Wishlist confirmation toast | 2 | 2.0 | 3.5 | **Reversal of SFCC-434, not a duplicate** |
| SFCC-724 | Indexable filter pages | 5 | 5.25 | 16.0 | **UNSIZEABLE** — URL shape undecided |
| SFCC-804 | Wallet marketing opt-in | 2 | 0.0 | 3.25 | **NOT ESTIMABLE** — placeholder story |
| SFCC-857 | Emarsys Web Extend | 3 | 6.0 | 6.0 | UNDER — no tracking layer exists |
| SFCC-858 | Live-chat co-browsing | 3 | 4.5 | 4.5 | UNDER — that's a floor, not a ceiling |
| SFCC-859 | Field validation / regex | 5 | 8.0 | 8.0 | UNDER — 6 form hooks need copy-first |
| SFCC-866 | Cart→wishlist auto-remove | 2 | 0.25 | 1.5 | OVER — cheapest folded into SFCC-272 now |
| SFCC-946 | Avalara scope expansion | 2 | 0.5 | 0.75 | **MIS-ATTRIBUTED** — payload-driven |
| SFCC-950 | VIP rewards via Global-E | 3 | 0.0 | 2.0 | **MIS-ATTRIBUTED** — vendor iframe |
| | **Total** | **49.0** | **52.9** | **87.8** | vs **7.5 remaining** |

---

## 2. Defects in the capacity tables themselves

- **SFCC-142 is recorded twice, differently.** Main table `FED+BED 5, QA 3`; capacity table `FED 3.5 + DEV 3.5 = 7, QA 2`. Two dev-days appear or vanish depending on which table you read. It's a scope disagreement — 2.5 is credible as "delta on an existing order page", 3.5 as "includes standing the page up". Nobody wrote down which was meant.
- **SFCC-155 consumes Phase 1 capacity for non-Phase-1 work.** Booked as FED 1 + DEV 1 while its own note says "Not for Phase 1". Tash is flagged to fix the table; it hasn't happened.
- **SFCC-173 is booked as 3 consumed FED days while its status is still TBC.**
- **The even-split convention is unreliable.** It was applied to SFCC-155 and SFCC-143 but *not* to SFCC-142. For SFCC-135 it's actively wrong — `projectState.md:163` records the BED half as "SFCC OOTB configuration only", i.e. provisioning, not build. Nearly all the remaining work is front-end.

---

## 3. The five rows that aren't estimate problems

**SFCC-946 (Avalara) may not be chargeable scope at all.** Three docs give three different answers on which markets Avalara already covers, and the most recent — **PRC-07, signed off by Emma/Rebecca on 24 June** — already puts **AU, EU, US and UK** in the go-live baseline. That is exactly what SFCC-946 proposes to "expand" into. Separately the FE work is near zero: `order-summary` isn't overridden and base renders `basket.taxTotal` straight from the payload, identically whichever engine computed it. Real FE tax work is already ticketed as SFCC-462 and SFCC-43.

**SFCC-950 reverses a signed-off requirement.** `checkout.md:221` PAY-039: *"HK, ME, EU International: Retail Rewards **cannot** be redeemed online."* `account.md:289` logs CRM-022 as Open, "not currently scoped". The deliverable also lives inside Global-E's own iframe, and the data handoff is server-side SendCart, already spec'd under PRC-16. The ticket's own note says there are no legacy gold VICs internationally — zero affected customers.

**SFCC-174 duplicates SFCC-572**, which sits in epic SFCC-22 with **7 real acceptance criteria**. More broadly there are **two parallel SEO backlogs**: SFCC-724 ≈ SFCC-563 + SFCC-577, and SFCC-563 carries the *same* `DMU-023` label. Sizing the Enhancements copies books the same days twice. Deciding that the Enhancements epic owns no SEO work would recover ~6 FED days — most of the gap.

**SFCC-156 is not a duplicate of SFCC-135.** Jira records the link as **`Blocks`**, not Duplicate, and the ticket ("Duplicate Account Prevention & Apple Hide My Email") is **High**, carries CRM-005/033/034, and has **7 ACs**, three of them front-end. Marking it N/A doesn't remove ~2–3 FED days; it pushes them silently into SFCC-135's 7.

**SFCC-710 is a reversal, not a duplicate.** The tracker asks Jasmijn to check for duplication. There is none — but `product-detail/index.tsx:590` says verbatim: *"SFCC-434 — toast-free add… **Jasmijn confirmed the PDP badge has no confirmation message**, only the icon state change."* SFCC-710 asks for that message back.

---

## 4. Two live defects found while auditing

Neither is an estimate issue. Both are in shipped or shipping code.

### 4a. `/social-callback` has no registered route — social sign-in cannot complete

`social.enabled: true` on **dev, test, sit, uat, staging and production** (`config/*.js`), and `redirectURI` defaults to `/social-callback`. `overrides/app/ssr.js:115` already allowlists `^/social-callback`, so the path was expected to resolve.

But it never gets registered. `overrides/app/routes.tsx:15` imports the **static named export** `{routes as _routes}` and spreads it at line 90. The social route is appended only inside the base **default export function** (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes.jsx:131-157`), which nothing calls — our own default export at `routes.tsx:114` runs `configureRoutes(routes, …)` on the static array.

A shopper returning from Apple or Google would fall through to the `/:segments+` catch-all, resolve `social-callback` as a category, and land on not-found. `loginIDPUser` never runs. The social buttons in the wishlist auth drawer are already built and shipped.

*Verified statically, not exercised in a running environment. Worth a 5-minute confirmation on a preview target before anyone acts on it.*

### 4b. SFCC-947 is a real a11y defect, dismissed by pointing at the ticket that caused it

The row says *"Not an enhancement — Jasmijn has a ticket and is being built"* → SFCC-101. It's the other way round: **SFCC-101 shipped the pattern SFCC-947 objects to, and it's on `develop`.**

In `zimmSizeSelector/index.tsx` on `origin/develop`, "Find your size" renders twice, both calling the same handler — at **line 167** (`triggerRowRight`, the placement SFCC-947 recommends keeping) and again at **lines 210–214**, inside the dropdown in a `<div>` that is a **sibling of `<ul role="listbox">`**. SFCC-101's **AC9 mandates the second one**, so the two tickets conflict at AC level.

The panel drives selection through `focusedIndex` within the `ul`, so the two links sit outside that keyboard model — either unreachable while the panel is open, or Tab-reachable in a way that pulls focus out of the composite widget mid-selection. A screen reader announces "Find your size" twice with nothing to distinguish them. WCAG 2.2 AA, 2.1.1 and 4.1.2.

~2–3 FED days to remediate, but the AC9 decision has to land first. Worth settling before SFCC-101 clears SIT.

---

They price the *feature*, not this codebase's cost of change.

- **No `overrides/app/pages/account/` exists.** 6,300 LOC of base account pages untouched. SFCC-142, 143, 710 and part of 859 all land there, and none of them carries the copy-first conversion.

- **Didomi is not built** — 5 runtime dependencies in `package.json`, none consent-related; `config/sit.js:46` says so in a comment. It gates SFCC-857 and SFCC-858, and it's unscheduled.
- **No tracking layer at all** — no `dataLayer`, no `gtag`. SFCC-857's 3 days price a script drop-in; the event mapping is all net-new.

One correction to a premise used widely in planning: `config/sites.overlay.js` defines **11 PWA site configs over 8 SFCC sites** (EU domestic is four single-locale PWA sites on one SFCC site). Each is pinned to one locale. For FED work the multiplier is **11**.

description: overrides/app/routes.tsx imports base's STATIC routes array, so any route base appends conditionally in its default export (social-callback) is silently never registered
metadata:
