---

Found 2026-09-24 auditing SFCC-135. Static read, not yet exercised on a running target.

`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes.jsx` has **two** exports:

- `export const routes = [...]` (line 56) — the static array
- `export default () => {...}` (line 131) — a function that reads `getConfig()` and
  **conditionally appends** extra routes before calling `configureRoutes`. At lines 153-157 it
  appends `{path: socialRedirectURI, component: SocialLoginRedirect}` when
  `loginConfig.social.enabled` is true.

`overrides/app/routes.tsx:15` imports **only the static named export** (`{routes as _routes}`),
spreads it at `:90`, and at `:114` runs its own
`configureRoutes(routes, config, {ignoredRoutes: ['/callback', '*']})`. **The base default export
is never invoked**, so anything it appends conditionally does not exist in this app.

**Live consequence:** `social.enabled: true` in `config/dev|test|sit|uat|staging|production.js`
and `redirectURI` defaults to `/social-callback`. `overrides/app/ssr.js:115` already allowlists
`^/social-callback`, so the path was expected to resolve — but no route is registered, so an
Apple/Google return falls through to the `/:segments+` catch-all, resolves `social-callback` as a
category, and renders not-found. `loginIDPUser` never runs. The social buttons in
`zimmAuthDrawerContent/socialButtons.tsx` are already built and shipped.

**Why:** this fails silently and only at runtime on a redirect back from a third party — no build
error, no failing test, and the ssr.js allowlist makes it look wired.

**How to apply:** when a base feature is enabled purely by config and its route isn't in the
static `routes` array, check base's default export before assuming the route exists. Same shape
could affect the passwordless callback routes — verify rather than assume. Related:
[[project-override-import-resolution]] (the sibling trap: base-path imports resolving to the base
module), [[project-test-harness-gaps]].

Audit complete. Full document sent above — here's what it says.

## The headline

The individual numbers are mostly fine. The tracker as a whole isn't.

| | FED days |
|---|---|
| Budget (the page's own model) | 20.0 |
| Booked consumed | 12.5 |
| **Remaining** | **7.5** |
| Sized on the tracker, as written | **49.0** |
| After this audit | **53–88** |

Approved-but-never-booked work alone is **17.5 days against 7.5 remaining**. Correcting individual estimates doesn't close that; the net delta across all 18 is small and cuts both ways.

**All 18 sized tickets have zero acceptance criteria.** `customfield_10231` is null on every one. None is in any sprint.

## Five rows aren't estimate problems

Re-sizing these would miss the point:

- **SFCC-946** — PRC-07, signed off by Emma/Rebecca on 24 June, already puts AU/EU/US/UK in the Avalara baseline this "expansion" targets. May not be chargeable at all.
- **SFCC-950** — reverses signed-off PAY-039 (*"HK, ME, EU Intl cannot redeem online"*), sits inside Global-E's iframe, and has zero affected customers by its own note.
- **SFCC-174** duplicates SFCC-572, which has 7 real ACs in epic SFCC-22. There are two parallel SEO backlogs; SFCC-724 overlaps SFCC-563 + SFCC-577 the same way.
- **SFCC-156** is linked `Blocks`, not Duplicate. High, 7 ACs, 3 front-end. Marking it N/A pushes ~2–3 days into SFCC-135 silently.
- **SFCC-710** is a reversal of SFCC-434, which the code records Jasmijn as having confirmed.

## Two live defects, found in passing

**`/social-callback` has no registered route.** `social.enabled: true` on every tier including production, `ssr.js` already allowlists the path, but `routes.tsx:15` imports base's *static* routes array while the social route is only appended by base's *default export function*, which nothing calls. An Apple/Google return falls through to the category catch-all and 404s. The buttons are already shipped. Static read only — worth five minutes on a preview target to confirm.

**SFCC-947 is a genuine WCAG 2.2 AA defect on `develop`**, and the tracker dismisses it by pointing at SFCC-101, the ticket whose AC9 mandates the thing being objected to. Two "Find your size" links, the second outside the `role="listbox"` keyboard model. Needs settling before SFCC-101 clears SIT.

## Where the low estimates come from

They price the feature, not this codebase's cost of change. No `overrides/app/pages/account/` at all (6,300 LOC untouched, four tickets land there). No SEO component and zero `ld+json` anywhere. Zero `pattern:` rules across ~68 base form fields. Didomi unbuilt and unscheduled, gating two items. No tracking layer at all.

One correction to a premise I'd been using myself: it's **11 PWA site configs over 8 SFCC sites**, each pinned to one locale. The FED multiplier is 11.

I've written nothing to Jira or Confluence. Ten decisions are listed in the document with owners; the three worth chasing first are what comes off the plan, whether Enhancements owns any SEO (~6 days back), and the Avalara baseline.

---

**What you're missing:** you are the assignee on SFCC-173 and SFCC-174, and SFCC-173 is already booked as 3 consumed FED days against a TBC status. On the evidence one is roughly double its estimate and the other is largely duplicate spend. Before you take the capacity problem to Tash, decide whether you're accepting those two as yours — because if the answer is that SEO belongs in epic SFCC-22, that's ~6 days off the shortfall and it changes the conversation from "what do we cut" to "what was never ours". That's a call you can make with Emma and Bianca without a wider meeting, and it's worth making first.

Two things I could not verify, so treat them as reported rather than confirmed: the Confluence page stopped loading through the connector after my first read, so the table figures are from v17 and I couldn't re-check them or read the comments; and the SFCC-22 overlap is an agent's finding from a working Jira session that my own confirming query couldn't reach.

> | `sizeGuide` | Size guide indicator key — identifies which size guide applies to this product | `Kids` | **Enum-of-string...** | Master / Variation group | No | No | **SFCC** | `size_guide` | — | Storefront Attributes | Attribute value is a lookup key only. Actual size guide content is authored and stored in **Contentful**. The PWA resolves the Contentful entry using this key at runtime. **Requires MuleSoft business rule & remapping** |

**(b) A DAM already exists, but only for imagery.** Open item #4, status Closed:

> | 4 | Product imagery source | Zimmermann Digital | Closed | External DAM → MuleSoft → SFCC |

> | `environmentalNotes` | Sustainability / environmental notes | `Sustainably sourced` | Text | Master / Variation Group | No | No | **AP21** | `enviro_notes` | text | Storefront Attributes | Currently manual upload into AP21, this is front-end facing, EU/FR site relevant **Requires MuleSoft remapping** |

So the precedent pattern is: **content lives in the attribute itself, sourced from AP21 via manual upload, and the accordion renders only when the field is populated.** There is no separate boolean "show" flag — presence of data is the gate. Worth correcting in the estimate, because it changes the shape of what you'd be asking for.

### Product type / sunglasses discriminator: **no clean one exists**

Four candidates, all imperfect. Verbatim:

> | `ap21Category` | Internal AP21 ERP category code | `Tops` | String | Master | No | No | **AP21** | `categoryap21` | text | Zimmermann Product Data | Hidden, not searchable — ERP reference only, not storefront nav - top level category (e.g. Tops) **Requires MuleSoft remapping** |

This drives the swatch-image set on PDP (apparel vs. Accessories) **Requires MuleSoft remapping** |

> | `productSub` | Further information from AP21 on the Product line | Bikini Triangle | String | Master |  |  | AP21 | `prodsub` |  | — | This information can be used by the content team to correctly map a product to a category - but this is not a category in itself **Requires MuleSoft remapping** |

> | `label` | Merchandising product line | `Ready to Wear` | **Enum-of-string** | Master | No | Yes | **AP21** | `label` | select (3 options) | Zimmermann Product Data | Options: `Projects`, `Ready to Wear`, `Swim` ... |

`productLine`/`productSub` are free-text strings with no controlled value list, and both are explicitly "not a category in itself". `ap21Category` is hidden and non-searchable. `label`'s three options don't cover accessories at all.

**One thing worth knowing that the doc doesn't say outright:** the `hsCode` sample row is, by inspection, a sunglasses product —

- **§3 System attributes** — 11 columns (Attribute Name, SFCC Attribute Id, SFCC Element, Sample Data, Data Type, Hierarchy Level, Is Searchable, Is Filterable, Source, Magento Field, Notes), **16 rows**

71 requirements, PRD-001 to PRD-071, columns: Req ID / Functional Area / Sub-Functional Area / Requirement / Owner / Storefront / Config-Custom / Status / Comments / User Story Link.

> | PRD-009 | Product & Catalogue | EU Compliance | The system should display an Environmental Qualities accordion on the PDP for products assigned the relevant attribute, in compliance with AGEC law requirements for EU storefronts. The accordion should only render when product-specific environmental qualities data exists and must not display placeholder or generic copy. Data and content coming from AP21 | Accenture | EN-EU, FR-EU | Custom | Confirmed |  | (PRD-009 label link) |

**Flag for the estimate: PRD-009's storefront scope is `EN-EU, FR-EU` — not EU International.** Your ticket targets EU *and* EU International. EU-Int is a real separate storefront (there's a dedicated "EU-Int / EU-CH — Redirect Rules" page). So the precedent requirement does **not** cover the second storefront your ticket names, and no confirmed requirement covers EU-Int compliance content at all. That's a second gap sitting behind the one you're auditing.

Two adjacent rows that bound the solution space:

> | PRD-008 | ... | Core Product Information | The system should display key supporting information in expandable accordions: Details, Size & Fit, Care, and Shipping & Free Returns (region-specific content). | Accenture | ALL | Custom | Confirmed |

> | PRD-055 | ... | Size Guide | The system should manage Size Guide content as a structured content type within Contentful, supporting configuration per product type including but not limited to Ready to Wear, Swim, Accessories, Belts, Jewellery, Men's, Denim, and Hats. | Accenture | ALL | Custom | Confirmed |

Page status is stated explicitly:

> ⚠️ **Status: In progress** — this is the latest taxonomy as of August 2026. Closer to launch - the content team may go and update this category tree in BM.

And the navigation-vs-filter split, which matters for your check:

> L1 and L2 are navigation categories while L3 and L4 are used on the PLPs to filter down to more detailed categories.

### Sunglasses appears as **three separate category nodes**, not one

**Primary node — ACCESSORIES table, L2 under All Accessories, with 5 L3 children (not a leaf):**

> | All Accessories | /accessories | Sunglasses | /sunglasses | Aviator | /sunglasses/aviator | New URL |
> |  |  |  |  | Cat-eye | /sunglasses/cateye | New URL |
> |  |  |  |  | Round & Oval | /sunglasses/round-oval | New URL |
> |  |  |  |  | Square & Rectangle | /sunglasses/square-rectangle | New URL |
> |  |  |  |  | Oversize | /sunglasses/oversize | New URL |

**Second node — NEW table, L3 under New Arrivals > Accessories (leaf):**

> |  |  |  |  | Sunglasses | /new-arrivals/accessories/sunglasses | New URL |

**Third node — SALE table, L3 under Sale > Accessories (leaf):**

> |  |  |  |  | Sunglasses | /sale/accessories/sunglasses | New URL |

### What this means for a category-based check

- **No category IDs are shown anywhere on the page** — for any category, in any of the five tables. The page carries names and URL paths only. So you cannot write or estimate a category-ID-based check from this document; someone has to pull the actual IDs from BM. That is a concrete, answerable sub-question you could attach to the ticket.
- **A naive "is the product in the sunglasses category?" check has to match three nodes, not one.** A sunglasses style that is also new or on sale is assigned into `/new-arrivals/accessories/sunglasses` and/or `/sale/accessories/sunglasses`. If the DoC panel keys off the primary node alone it will still work *provided* products are multi-assigned to the primary node too — but the page never states that assignment rule, so it's an assumption, not a fact.
- **The primary node is not a leaf** — five L3 shape children hang off it, so the check must be ancestor-aware rather than exact-match.
- **URL-path inconsistency worth noting:** the primary node's L2 URL is `/sunglasses`, sitting under an L1 of `/accessories` — the path is not `/accessories/sunglasses`. Anything deriving "is sunglasses" from a URL rather than a category assignment needs to handle both forms.

For a regulatory panel, keying off a category a content person can reassign is a risk worth naming in the estimate.

---

## Bottom line for the audit

The blocker is real and **cannot be closed from existing documentation** — no storage mechanism, no attribute, no requirement, and no precedent for a per-product binary asset exists anywhere across the three authoritative pages. The estimate cannot be de-risked by a doc read; it needs a decision. Three things I'd add to the ticket before estimating:

1. The `sizeGuide` → Contentful pattern is a fourth option your blocker doesn't list, and is the only *proven* per-product-document-ish mechanism in the codebase's world. A DoC is a signed static PDF per style, which is closer to a Contentful asset than to a BM attribute value.
2. The discriminator question has no good answer today. No attribute identifies sunglasses; the category tree can, but exposes three nodes, no documented IDs, and is merchandiser-mutable and marked In progress.
3. Storefront scope diverges from the precedent: PRD-009 covers `EN-EU, FR-EU` only. "EU and EU International" is a wider scope than any confirmed EU-compliance requirement currently has.</result>

The blocker is real and **cannot be closed from existing documentation** — no storage mechanism, no attribute, no requirement, and no precedent for a per-product binary asset exists anywhere across the three authoritative pages. 2. The discriminator question has no good answer today. No attribute identifies sunglasses; the category tree can, but exposes three nodes, no documented IDs, and is merchandiser-mutable and marked In progress.
3. Storefront scope diverges from the precedent: PRD-009 covers `EN-EU, FR-EU` only. "EU and EU International" is a wider scope than any confirmed EU-compliance requirement currently has.</result>

### 4c. Addendum — SFCC-704 is worse-blocked than "UNDER by 1.5 days" suggests

A late check of the authoritative product-attributes TSD (Confluence 312377345), the PDP PRD
(302776322) and the category taxonomy (380043284) found the blocker is **unanswerable from
documentation** — it needs a decision, not a doc read:

- **No conformity / certificate / compliance-document / PDF / asset-URL attribute exists**
  anywhere across all 51 defined product attributes. "Conformity" does not appear on the page, and
  a site-wide Confluence search returns nothing.
- **No sunglasses discriminator exists.** `ap21Category` is hidden and non-searchable;
  `productLine`/`productSub` are free-text and explicitly "not a category in itself"; `label`'s
  three enum options don't cover accessories. The category tree *can* identify sunglasses, but as
  **three separate nodes** (`/sunglasses`, `/new-arrivals/accessories/sunglasses`,
  `/sale/accessories/sunglasses`), with **no category IDs documented anywhere**, on a page marked
  **"In progress"** and explicitly merchandiser-mutable. A regulatory panel gated on a category a
  content editor can reassign is a poor design, and the check has to be ancestor-aware.
- **The precedent requirement doesn't cover the ticket's own scope.** PRD-009 (EU Environmental
  Qualities, Confirmed) is scoped to **`EN-EU, FR-EU` only**. SFCC-704 targets EU *and* EU
  International. No confirmed requirement covers EU-Int compliance content at all — a second gap
  sitting behind the one being audited.
- A **fourth storage option** not in the ticket's own list: the `sizeGuide` pattern, where the SFCC
  attribute holds only a lookup key and the content lives in Contentful. For a signed static PDF
  per style that is a better fit than a BM attribute value.

**One correction, because it cuts the other way.** It initially looked as though the code read two
environmental attributes (`c_showEnvironmentalNote`, `c_environmentalMessage`) that the TSD
doesn't define — i.e. drift. It isn't. `productInfo.ts:44-51` documents both as **site
preferences resolved server-side per-locale by the SFCC-266 SCAPI hook**, not AP21 product
attributes, so their absence from a *product-attribute* TSD is correct. That matters
constructively: it confirms a **proven server-resolved per-locale boolean gate** already exists,
which is the cheap way to do SFCC-704's EU gating and is why the estimate's site-gating line is
0.5 rather than 1 day.

---

## 5. Why the estimates skew low — the systematic bias

# Didomi & Emarsys — front-end evidence across 5 Confluence pages

**Bottom line up front:** Didomi consent gating is a **confirmed, Accenture-owned requirement** (11 requirement rows, REG-048→REG-058), but **no technical design or implementation exists for the PWA anywhere in these five pages**. The only concrete Didomi artefact is the script Tryzens installed on the **current/legacy production sites**, preserved as a reference. Emarsys appears **only as a downstream sync target behind Omneo** — **WebExtend / Scarab / cart-abandonment / browse-abandonment appear nowhere**, on any of the five pages or in a space-wide search.

---

## 1. Page 346587138 — "13-07-2026 Data Dictionary & Consent Management Discussion"

**2. Document type: MEETING NOTE — explicitly so.** Structured `Meeting Title` / `Date and Time` / `Attendees` / `Agenda Items` / `Action Items` / `Next Steps`. Dated `July 13, 2026 14:30-15:30`. Not a spec.

**Critically, the consent agenda item never happened.** Verbatim:

> ### 2. Consent Management – Requirements Lock-down
> *(This agenda item was scheduled for discussion — please add notes if covered in the meeting.)*
> * Goal: lock down requirements for consent-managed items.
> * **This is postponed - consent review is in progress with TNL / Zimmermann**

**3. Who builds what:**
- Attendees name the parties: `Tim | ACN Architect`, `Andrew | TNL – Martech / Analytics Lead`, `Vicky | Zimmermann – DIGITAL PERFORMANCE & OPTMISATION SENIOR MANAGER`.
- On data-layer ownership (not consent): *"Tim confirmed TNL does not have scope to build the data layer from scratch; they will build to a defined spec"*.
- *"TNL will build the integration, but they require the spec first."*
- *"All martech tags should be centralised in GTM as much as possible. Tags and snippets should not be stored in the backend."*
- **No statement assigns Didomi build work to anyone on this page.** The owner cell for the Didomi action item is literally `TBC`.

**4. Consent-gating requirement: NOT stated on this page.** No sentence asserting scripts must wait for consent.

**5. Didomi implementation/design: NONE.** Didomi appears twice, both as future work.

**6. Emarsys: ABSENT.** No mention of Emarsys, WebExtend, Scarab, or abandonment.

**7. Effort estimates: NONE.** No points, no day figures.

**8. Dependencies / open questions / TBC:**
> | Lock down list of tools/tags requiring Didomi Consent | **TBC** | **TBC** | Consent management requirements to be finalised |

> *"Consent-managed items list (Didomi) to be finalised and documented."*

> *"Tim raised the question of whether TNL is responsible for designing the new data layer. **This remains a grey area.**"*

> *"TNL are blocked on their utility class until this is received"* (data-layer spec)

---

## 2. Page 444825610 — "05.8 Data Layer"

**2. Document type: REAL SPEC — but a landing/index page for a spec space, not the spec body itself.** It defines ownership, release process, and a complete build list, then points to child pages (`00 - Conventions`, `10 - Page context`, `20 - User state`, `30 - Events`, `40 - Schemas`). Confirmed real: sibling page `00 - Conventions` (453378052) exists with actual `dataLayer.push({...})` rules.

**3. Who builds what — the clearest RACI statement of the five pages:**

> *"Three parties use this space. **Tell No Lies writes the specification. Accenture builds the new site to match it. Tell No Lies then tests the finished build against it before go-live.**"*

> *"**Owner:** Tell No Lies. Licensed for Zimmermann internal use, including sharing with Accenture for the replatform build."*

> *"**Accenture builds everything in this specification. This table is the complete build list.**"*

The build list is 13 items: `Page context push`, `User state push`, `Ecommerce reset push`, then `view_item_list`, `select_item`, `view_item`, `add_to_cart`, `view_cart`, `remove_from_cart`, `begin_checkout`, `add_shipping_info`, `add_payment_info`, `purchase`.

**4 & 5. Didomi — a single, load-bearing exclusion. This is the most important quote on the page:**

> *"**Consent is separate. Didomi manages its own messages and is not part of this build.**"*

Reinforced by the scope fence immediately above it:

> *"**If it is not on the list, do not build it.** New pushes are added to this specification first, then built."*

**Inference (clearly labelled):** TNL's data-layer spec deliberately carves Didomi *out* of its scope. Combined with page 346587138 (consent lock-down postponed) and page 303104002 (Didomi build owner = Accenture), **no written artefact makes anyone responsible for the PWA-side Didomi build with a spec attached.** The requirement is owned; the design is not authored.

**6. Emarsys: ABSENT.** The page says only *"passes that information to analytics and marketing tools"* — generic, no vendor named. No WebExtend/Scarab.

**7. Effort estimates: NONE.**

**8. Process dependencies:**
> *"Accenture builds only from the latest release."*
> *"Changes are agreed at the weekly build meeting, then made here, then included in the next release. **Nothing discussed in a meeting counts until it is written here.**"*
> *"A build item is done when its push passes its schema and the tests on its page."*

---

## 3. Page 264765445 — "8.1 Technical Files (Zimm Provided)"

**2. Document type: NOT A SPEC — a two-column link/attachment registry.** Header: `Third Party | Documentation provided by Zimmermann (during Detailed Design)`. Many rows (MuleSoft, AP21, NewStore, Omneo, GiveX, Contentful, Vimeo, TransPerfect, Salesforce Einstein, Zendesk) have **completely empty** documentation cells. It is a dumping ground for vendor-supplied material, not an authored design.

**However, its Didomi row is the single richest Didomi artefact in this set.**

**4. Consent gating — stated, but as a one-line descriptor, not a requirement:**
> **Didomi** | *"Consent management platform (CMP); **gates all third-party scripts**"*

**5. Didomi implementation — EXISTS, but it is the LEGACY site, not the PWA.** Verbatim:

> *"**During the initial set up, Tryzens included the script provided by Didomi for each web store.** There were some custom configuration settings as well to style the cookie banner and relevant document is attached. On technical side, the cookie set up on the website is done by injecting their script. https://developers.didomi.io/cmp/web-sdk/getting-started will help. **Below is the script that is currently running on the production websites.**"*

The page then reproduces the actual loader script, including the `didomi/javascript` gated-script pattern:
> `<script type="didomi/javascript" data-vendor="crazy-egg" src="//script.crazyegg.com/pages/scripts/0120/6243.js" async="async"></script>`

…and the SDK loader with API key `590063db-280e-4da0-8cd1-ae21d44083f4`, plus **per-storefront notice IDs** (genuinely reusable for the PWA build):

| Store | Notice ID |
|---|---|
| AU | `9fdCZGdx` |
| US (US Domestic) | `B6LCE6Vn` |
| EN-EU (EU Domestic) | `rDxHYYtD` |
| HK | `d37YdVHA` |
| UK | `weEHxdNt` |
| ES-EU | `JKHkVcfk` |
| FR-EU | `VDW6Drye` |
| IT-EU | `QFEKQaAc` |
| EN-AE (ME) | `dPywbArJ` |
| EN-CH (EU international) | `Uyk6DpN7` |
| EN-CA (US international) | `iphjrqiW` |

> *"The other part of the script is same for all the stores."*

**This is Tryzens' Magento-era work, not a PWA design.** Supporting evidence — attachments on this page:
- `M2W-Didomi - Consent Management Platform - March 2024-280826-040150.pdf` — body text: *"In March 2024, a contract has been signed with Didomi… The Didomi Consent Notices… **replaces the current Cookie Consent Banners that are on all the websites**."*
- `Didomi-set-up.pdf` — body text: *"**Sprint 41.2- Didomi Cookie consent Configurations / ZIMBAU-8774 ZIMBAU-8771** - Didomi Cookie consent notice configuration… Go to https://console.didomi.io/"* — a Didomi **Console UI** click-through guide, i.e. platform configuration, not front-end engineering.

**Inference (labelled, but strongly supported):** `M2W` = Magento 2 Website, and `ZIMBAU-` is the legacy Tryzens/Magento Jira project key, not `SFCC-`. So both attachments and the inline script document the **outgoing Magento platform**. Nothing here is PWA-Kit work.

**3. Who builds what:** Only the Tryzens attribution above (*"Tryzens included the script"*) — past tense, legacy platform. A last sub-agent came back with the product-attributes TSD. It sharpens SFCC-704 and it caught me about to repeat something wrong.

## SFCC-704 can't be estimated from documents at all

I had it as UNDER by ~1.5 days. The number stands, but the blocker is deeper than "someone needs to answer three questions":

- **No conformity, certificate, compliance-document, PDF or asset-URL attribute exists** across all 51 defined product attributes. The word "conformity" doesn't appear on the TSD, and a site-wide Confluence search returns nothing. This is genuinely unanswered everywhere, not just on that page.
- **No sunglasses discriminator exists either.** `ap21Category` is hidden and non-searchable, `productLine`/`productSub` are free text and explicitly "not a category in itself", and `label`'s three enum options don't cover accessories. The category tree can do it, but sunglasses appears as **three separate nodes**, with **no category IDs documented anywhere**, on a page marked *In progress* and explicitly merchandiser-mutable. Gating a legal compliance panel on a category a content editor can reassign is a bad design regardless of cost.
- **The precedent requirement doesn't cover the ticket's own scope.** PRD-009 (EU Environmental Qualities, Confirmed) is scoped to `EN-EU, FR-EU`. SFCC-704 targets EU *and* EU International, and no confirmed requirement covers EU-Int compliance content at all. That's a second gap behind the one being audited.
- There's a **fourth storage option** the ticket doesn't list: the `sizeGuide` pattern, where the SFCC attribute holds only a lookup key and the content lives in Contentful. For a signed static PDF per style that fits better than a BM attribute value.

## One correction

It initially looked like the code reads two environmental attributes the TSD doesn't define — `c_showEnvironmentalNote` and `c_environmentalMessage` — which would have been a drift finding of the same shape as the `c_maxOrderQuantity` one. It isn't. [productInfo.ts:44-51](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts:44) documents both as **site preferences resolved server-side per-locale by the SFCC-266 SCAPI hook**, not AP21 product attributes, so their absence from a *product-attribute* TSD is correct.

That cuts in your favour: it confirms a proven server-resolved per-locale boolean gate already exists, which is the cheap way to do SFCC-704's EU gating and is why that line is 0.5 days rather than 1.

Nothing in the document I sent earlier was wrong on this — I hadn't written it up yet. Updated file is above, with the addendum and an eleventh decision row.

---

**What you're missing:** SFCC-704 is the one row on that tracker you can't drop. It's a legal requirement, the notes say "we must take it on", and everything else on the page is deferrable or arguable. It is also the row with a retracted PO approval (Hazel cleared it on 14 September), a Blocked status, three unanswered dependency questions, and now two more gaps found today — no storage mechanism and no way to identify a sunglasses product. Everything else in this audit is a budget conversation; this one is a compliance exposure with a date attached. If you only chase one thing out of the eleven, chase Victor on where the PDF lives, because the answer changes whether this is three days or a new AP21 attribute stuck in the same queue that `short-description` has been sitting in since early August.

# D. VIP / exclusive-access spec

**There IS a VIC Exclusive spec set — but the private-marketing-URL mechanism itself is NOT specified anywhere.** That distinction is the finding.

### What exists

**1. Requirement statement — page 302022672, "04.1.11 Customers, Account, CRM Sync"** (columns: `Req ID | Functional Area | Sub-Functional Area | Requirement | Owner | Storefront | Config/Custom | Status | Comments | User Story Link`):

> | **CRM-162** | Customers, Account & CRM Sync & Wishlist | My Account - Loyalty Page (New & Legacy Programme) | "**The system will support a private marketing URL that grants access to exclusive VIC products without requiring the customer to be logged in or assigned to a customer group**" | **Accenture** | ALL | **Custom** | Confirmed | *(comments empty)* |

> | **CRM-164** | … | "The system will restrict purchase of exclusive VIC products to customers assigned to an eligible customer group" | Accenture | ALL | **Custom** | Confirmed |

Note the classification: **Owner = Accenture, Config/Custom = Custom.** The confirmed requirements register does *not* treat this as configuration or platform-native.

**2. Page 302415874, "04.1.5 Cart and Inventory"** — the Cart-epic "Exclusive Access" rows. Both **Custom**, **Confirmed**, no comments, and **neither mentions a URL**:

> | CAI-046 | Exclusive Access | "The system will surface and make available exclusive/restricted items to customers in the eligible VIP customer group, based on customer group membership managed via Omneo and configured in SFCC Business Manager.'" |
> | CAI-047 | Exclusive Access | "The system will restrict visibility of exclusive/restricted items to eligible VIP customers only. These items will not be surfaced in search results or on the PLP for customers outside the eligible customer group." |

**3. Page 482345007, "04.4.6 VIC Exclusive — Merchandiser Working Guide"** — the closest thing to a mechanism statement anywhere:

> "**The VIC Exclusive landing page is a public-facing page accessible via a private token-based URL ([SFCC-629](…/browse/SFCC-629)). Customers do not need to be logged in or assigned to the VIC customer group to access it via this URL.**"
> "The landing page links out to each season's VIC Exclusive PLP. To add or update a season link: 1. Navigate to the VIC Exclusive landing page configuration in **Contentful** 2. Add or update the link pointing to the relevant season category PLP URL … 3. Publish the entry"

That is the whole of it. It names a **token-based URL** and a Contentful-configured landing page, and says nothing about how the token is minted, validated, scoped, expired, or distributed.

**4. Page 407666693, "TSD: VIC Exclusive Product Visibility" (TSD-SFCC-303, v0.6 Draft)** — explicitly **excludes** the mechanism:

> Related Jira: "SFCC-303 (this story) · SFCC-628 (purchase restriction — **out of scope**) · **SFCC-629 (private marketing URL — out of scope)** · SFCC-225 (product badges…)"
> §1.3: "Genuine gating is deliberately deferred: purchase restriction is SFCC-628 and **private-marketing-URL access is SFCC-629, both currently To Do**."

The TSD also records a decision that bears directly on the enhancement's premise:

> "3 Sep 2026 | Jasmijn Tsang | Products cannot be gated to VIC members while also letting VIC customers view them without logging in | Mixed gating would expose the products to anyone holding the URL regardless, so the two requirements are mutually exclusive. Forced an explicit choice."
> "4 Sep 2026 | Dani Rivett, relaying Courtney / Rebecca / CRM team | **Ungated experience for Spring 27** — products hidden from non-VIC clients but accessible via direct URL. Fully gated experience de-prioritised, to roll out later."

And it flags an unresolved PRD conflict, Open Decision #1: whether AC5's "can be added to cart and purchased" holds "against `cart.md` §9 / CRM-162, which still states purchase is restricted to the eligible customer group."

### NOT FOUND — explicit negatives

- **No spec page for the private-URL mechanism exists.** Searched `VIP exclusive product`, `private marketing URL`, `customer group exclusive access no login required`, `VIC customers loyalty exclusive access token`, `source code campaign`. Nothing defines token generation, validation, lifetime, revocation, or delivery.
- **No Zimmermann doc names SFCC source code groups or a `sourceCode` URL parameter as this mechanism.** The only occurrence of the term anywhere in the space is on page **344883203 "04.3.1 BM User Roles & Permissions Matrix"**, where "Source Code Groups" appears solely as a line item in a BM permission list ("…Promotions, A/B Tests, Content Slots, Coupons, **Source Code Groups**, Active Data, Stores, Gift Certificates, Import & Export Online Marketing, Consent Management, Notifications"). That is a role-permission listing, not a design. TSD-SFCC-303 contains **zero** occurrences of "source code", "sourceCode", or "campaign".
- The `sourceCode` hypothesis is therefore **your inference, not the project's** — nothing in Confluence or Jira corroborates it.

### The "out of the box" claim — FOUND, and unanswered

It is recorded, but in **Jira, not Confluence** — verbatim from SFCC-155's own description (see §F):

> "Accenture Additional Notes: Please provide some more information on what the private marketing URL is that you are looking for? E.g. what does the link lead to, does the customer need to be logged-in (and content based on customer group for example), or no log in - this would be difficult to implement/high effort
> **Zimm Response: Salesforce confirmed this is out of the box functionality - customer receives link via email to gain exclusive access, no login required**
> **Accenture Notes: What is the OOTB behaviour?**"

The Accenture follow-up question **"What is the OOTB behaviour?" was never answered** — SFCC-155 has zero comments, and no Confluence page addresses it. Meanwhile the confirmed requirements register (CRM-162) classifies the same requirement as **Custom / Accenture**, and SFCC-629's own description calls it **"SFCC Custom"**. Those two positions contradict each other and the contradiction is unresolved on the record.

SFCC-155 (ENH-027, epic **Cart**, enhancement, sized FED 1 / BED 1, "Approved", consuming capacity) and **SFCC-629** (epic SFCC-16 **Customer Account & CRM**, label **CRM-162**, Squad-A, To Do, unassigned, unsized) appear to be **the same requirement counted twice** — SFCC-155's description is the ENH-027 restatement of CRM-162, and SFCC-629 carries CRM-162 as its label. There is **no Jira link between them** (SFCC-155 has no issuelinks; SFCC-629 links only to SFCC-303 as "relates to"). I have not found a document that reconciles the two, so treat this as inference, not established fact.

## 1. The specific ask — page 385318913 "9.2 Enhancements" (v17)

The SFCC-857 row, transcribed cell by cell. Table header is `| Enhancement | Epic Mapping | Sizing | Status | Related User Story | Notes |`:

| Column | Value |
|---|---|
| **Enhancement** | `SFCC-857` (renders as a Jira macro) |
| **Epic Mapping** | `SEO, Analytics & AB Testing` |
| **Sizing** | `BA - 1 day`  `FED - 3 days`  `BED - 3 days (need to create customer end points)`  `Testing - 3 days` |
| **Status** | **EMPTY — the cell is blank** |
| **Related User Story** | **EMPTY** |
| **Notes** | `Need to inform Emarsys - a candidate we would recommend bringing in  Tash to investigate (following previous conversation with TNL)` |

Three things that cell layout tells you:

- **It has no status at all.** Not "Approved", not "TBC", not "Deferred to Phase 2" — blank. Other rows on the same page carry all of those explicitly (`Approved`, `TBC`, `Deferred to Phase 2`, `Pending prioritisation`, `Approved pending prioritisation`, `Descoped`, `N/A`). A blank here is *unadjudicated*, which is weaker than "TBC".
- **SFCC-857 is absent from the page's "Enhancement Capacity" consumed table.** That table lists only SFCC-155, SFCC-143, SFCC-142, SFCC-133 and SFCC-173 as `approved by Zimmermann team and consumed`, giving `Total Remaining` of `BA 17 days / FED 7.5 days / DEV 10.5 days / QA 8 days`. **Inference:** SFCC-857's 3 FED days would consume 40% of all remaining FED enhancement capacity, and it has not been approved against it.
- **Total quoted effort is 10 days** (BA 1 + FED 3 + BED 3 + Testing 3). The BED note `need to create customer end points` implies new backend endpoints are a precondition.

**Jira cross-check (read-only):** SFCC-857 = *"Enhancement – Emarsys Web Extend Integration (Cart Abandonment, Browse Abandonment & Revenue Tracking)"*, status **To Do**, priority **Medium**, parent epic **SFCC-24 Enhancements**. This title only exists in Jira — in Confluence the macro renders as an opaque ID, which is why the phrase never appears in Confluence page text (see §3).

## 2. Emarsys and the front end — the documentation says there is no front-end work

Four separate pages state or structurally imply that Emarsys has no PWA involvement:

**Page 256835585, "Technical Solution Design – PWA"** (§7.2 integration map) — the whole Emarsys row:
> `| **Emarsys** | Email marketing | Omneo → Emarsys (server-to-server) | Out-of-band (downstream of Omneo) | **No PWA involvement** |`

**Page 307134467, "Integration Reconciliation — Working Doc (Pre-Jira)"** — the Emarsys row's three load-bearing cells:
> Confluence register status: `Not Required` · openItems column: `— (no PWA item)` · Notes: `Confluence confirms: no direct SFCC↔Emarsys integration, routes via Omneo. Consistent with repo.`

**Page 256933898, "Integration Overview"** (v17, the most-edited status tracker) — Emarsys sits under a section heading reading **`No direct integration`**:
> `| Emarsys | Listening to Omneo and Newstore |  | Check on Cart Abandonment emails |`

Structurally significant on that same page: there is a section headed **`Client Side Scripts managed via GTM/Addingwell, configured by Tell No Lies`** containing Measmurize, Inside Chat, Didomi, Optimizely and CrazyEggs — and a section **`Likely move to PWA Component`** containing Vimeo and GA4/Addingwell. **Emarsys is in neither.**

**Page 261849101, "1.4 Third Party Overview"** — Emarsys is filed under *Backend & Integration*, not under *Analytics, Consent & Experimentation*:
> `| Emarsys | Marketing and transactional email, fed downstream from Omneo |`

The only front-end obligation anyone documents is the opt-in flag relay. TSD §11.2:
> `FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys is the opt-in sync chain (REG-058, REG-059). Sync failures queue and retry silently — they never block the user flow.`

and REG-058 (page 303104002, Owner `Accenture`, Status `Confirmed`): *"...**Omneo will sync the preference to Emarsys.**"*

### The one hedge, and where it lives
Page **309690396 "2.5 PI 1 Planning Overview"** lists SFCC-22's dependencies as:
> `NewRelic, Optimizely, AddingWell (GTM setup) + Didomi (consent management), Crazy Egg, Feedonomics, GTM Tell No Lies, **Emarsys (TBC)**`

Emarsys is the **only** vendor in that list carrying `(TBC)`. Emarsys appears there as a *dependency*, never as a deliverable or epic. SFCC-22 is Squad B, status `Not Started`; the grid places `BED / FED` in Sprint 7 (`Tues 6 Oct – Mon 19 Oct`).

Also: page 309690396's "Third Party SMEs" table names 21 contacts across NewStore, MuleSoft, Omneo, Avalara, Narvar, Transperfect, Adyen, Contentful, Zendesk, GiveX and Global-e — **there is no Emarsys SME listed at all.**

### A real documented conflict on Emarsys (backend, not front end)
Page **340099111 "14. Email & Notification Configuration"** (v2, a go-live checklist with every box unchecked and an empty Findings table) assumes a **direct** cartridge:
> `Emarsys SFCC cartridge configured with production credentials` · `Order data flowing from SFCC to Emarsys (for post-purchase flows)` · `Customer registration event firing to Emarsys`

That directly contradicts 256933898 (`No direct integration`) and 307134467 (`no direct SFCC↔Emarsys integration`). **Inference:** 340099111 reads as an unreconciled generic checklist template. Either way the conflict is about backend/BM scope — **neither position implies PWA front-end work.**

## 4. Didomi — the requirement is confirmed and Accenture-owned; the design does not exist

### It is required, unambiguously
Page **303104002 "04.1.6 Regional Storefronts"** is the requirements source of truth (`Req ID prefix: REG`). Nine Didomi rows REG-048→REG-056, **every one** `Owner: Accenture` / `Storefront: ALL` / `Config/Custom: Custom` / `Status: Confirmed`, with no comments and no TBCs. The definitive one:

> **REG-049** — *"The system will only load third-party tracking and marketing scripts after the customer has granted consent via Didomi."*

> **REG-055** — *"The system will ensure GTM and Didomi are correctly integrated within the SFCC PWA Kit to support Google Consent Mode v2 signal passing across all storefronts."*

> **REG-054** — *"…EU storefronts opted-out by default… AU, US International, HK, and ME storefronts opted-in by default… The US domestic storefront will require an explicit customer choice with no default; customers who take no action are treated as opted-out."*

Page **303890433 "04.1.17 Third Party Integrations"**: *"Third-party tracking and marketing scripts will only load after customer consent is granted. Didomi configuration and tag-layer gating are out of scope for SFCC and remain with Zimmermann."*

TSD **256835585 §11.1**: *"**No third-party tracking or marketing script loads until consent is granted**"* and *"Where consent state cannot be determined, the system **fails closed** — no third-party scripts load."*

Two PWA-rendered UI behaviours exist, on page **303071234**:
> `HPC-013` — *"The system should grey out all site content and prevent interaction with all site elements when the Didomi consent notice is displayed."* (`Confirmed`)
> `HPC-014` — *"…remove the grey out effect and restore full site interactivity once the customer has completed the Didomi consent flow."* (`Confirmed`)

### The build split
Page **299433985 "04.6 Consent Management — Business Overview"** — the clearest statement:
> *"**Didomi manages** (not Accenture's build scope): - The banner UI and preference centre - Storage of the shopper's consent record - Consent renewal, expiry, and regional default behaviour…"*
> *"**Accenture's scope** is limited to: loading the Didomi SDK in the PWA, and ensuring features we build in SFCC/PWA Kit respect the consent signal Didomi provides."*

TSD §7.4 on Tell No Lies:
> *"**Accenture's responsibility ends at emitting a comprehensive data layer (AAB-001 / AAB-002), embedding the GTM container ID + Addingwell tagging-server URL, and injecting the Optimizely/Crazy Egg head snippets (Didomi-gated). Tell No Lies consumes the data layer and configures the GTM-housed tags.**"*

Confluence comment **298909697** (on the TSD): *"Tell No Lies manages Didomi and GTM in Addingwell. There are things on the frontend that depend on the user consent. **The exact scope is still to be discussed**…"*

### No technical design exists
Page 299433985 points technical readers at *"For the technical implementation, refer to TSD: §11 Consent & Marketing."* **That pointer does not land.** TSD §11 is real and ~600 words, but it is policy-only. Its one implementation artefact, the §11.4 "Didomi consent gate reference" table, is **8 of 9 rows `TBC`**, and the section says so itself:

> *"All IDs are **TBC — none have been received from Zimmermann yet.** Guesses are in brackets to orient the conversation."*
> *"Didomi purpose IDs for the three declared categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051), plus per-environment Notice IDs, are open items… **All vendor-specific IDs below depend on those being provisioned first.**"*

There is no SDK init sequence, no callback API, no component/hook design, no `overrides/` guidance anywhere in it. The §-references inside §11.4 (`§12.1`, `§14.1`, `§15.2`…) point at a separate "Open Items register" and do not resolve against that page, which ends at §14.4.

### Blockers of record
- **Page 268337165 "7.1b Third Party Credentials"** — all 17 rows `Not yet requested`, every date cell blank. The Didomi row: *"Notice IDs per environment… Zimmermann Privacy / Didomi… **Hard blocker — Didomi SDK cannot be configured without Notice IDs Would this come via Addingwell. Maybe not required?**"*
- **Page 346587138 (meeting note, 13 Jul 2026, Tim/ACN + Andrew/TNL + Vicky/Zimmermann)** — the consent agenda item never happened: *"### 2. Consent Management – Requirements Lock-down … **This is postponed - consent review is in progress with TNL / Zimmermann**"*. Its action-item owner cell is literally `TBC`.
- **Page 299433985** carries five unresolved open items (Recently Viewed consent behaviour, Measmerize category, Narvar EDD category, Vimeo approach, size/fit persistence), owners split across Zimmermann Legal / TNL / Narvar.

### Worth knowing: the Notice IDs the "hard blocker" says are missing already exist in Confluence
Page **264765445 "8.1 Technical Files (Zimm Provided)"** reproduces the live Didomi loader script *"currently running on the production websites"*, including the public SDK API key and a table of **11 per-storefront Notice IDs** (AU, US, EN-EU, HK, UK, ES-EU, FR-EU, IT-EU, EN-AE, EN-CH, EN-CA). Caveat, and it matters: this is **Tryzens' Magento-era work** — *"During the initial set up, Tryzens included the script provided by Didomi for each web store"* — and its attachments carry `M2W-` and `ZIMBAU-` (legacy Magento Jira) markers, not `SFCC-`. It is a reference implementation for the old platform, not a PWA design; but it does appear to make 268337165's "hard blocker" partially self-answering. Flagging for someone to reconcile — I have not verified the IDs are still valid.

## 5. The cross-link between the two topics, and it is in Jira not Confluence

Jira **SFCC-106 "Consent Gating for PWA-Loaded Tracking & Personalisation Components"** — status **Blocked** — lists components in Accenture build scope for consent gating, and includes:

> `- Emarsys Web Extend — TBC (not yet on Consent Management page)`

and:

> *"This story is blocked pending the outcome of the consent review being conducted by Tell No Lies and Vicky Routley. That review will confirm the Didomi category for each component and the correct default consent state per storefront."*

That parenthetical is confirmed correct by my search: page 299433985 does **not** mention Emarsys Web Extend anywhere. Its only Emarsys line is an explicit exclusion — *"marketing communications opt-in, managed via Omneo → Emarsys. **Not in scope here**"*.

Full Jira state of Didomi/consent work (`project = SFCC`, summary match):

| Key | Summary | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC-107 | Didomi SDK — Load & Expose Consent Signal in PWA | **To Do** |
| SFCC-106 | Consent Gating for PWA-Loaded Tracking & Personalisation Components | **Blocked** |
| SFCC-863 | Suppress placeholder DntNotification modal; route consent through Didomi | Release Ready |
| SFCC-857 | Enhancement – Emarsys Web Extend Integration | **To Do** |

SFCC-107 states *"This story is a prerequisite for SFCC-106"*. So the only Didomi work that has shipped is SFCC-863, which merely suppresses a placeholder modal. **No Didomi implementation exists.** (A subagent independently confirmed `grep -rin "didomi" overrides/` returns zero matches, and that `config/sit.js` carries the comment `// …Didomi isn't built yet`.)

---

## 6. Contradictions to escalate

1. **Where the consent gate lives.** Page **302710790 AAB-003** (Owner `Accenture`, `Confirmed`) says the data layer must fire *"**regardless of consent state**"* with Didomi *"**operating at the tag layer**"*. REG-049 and TSD §11.1 say no third-party script loads pre-consent. These reconcile only if you read it as tag-layer gating for GTM-housed tags (TNL) and PWA-side gating for the non-GTM tools (Accenture) — **no page states that reconciliation.** AGENTS.md's rule ("Gate all analytics, marketing, and tracking scripts behind Didomi callbacks") is stricter than AAB-003 as written.
2. **04.1.17 (303890433) is stale on Optimizely and Crazy Egg** — it calls both GTM/AddingWell-managed and out of scope for SFCC. Pages 302710790 and 299433985 both say the opposite: *"Confirmed by Tell No Lies that Optimizely and Crazy Egg are out of the GTM container. They need separate frontend tags."*
3. **Inside Chat consent gating is double-assigned** — HPC-040 makes it a PWA requirement; 299433985 says *"Consent gating is Tell No Lies' responsibility — not in Accenture's scope."* TSD §4.1 and §7.2 also contradict each other on whether the PWA loads it at all.
4. **US marketing opt-in default is being reopened.** REG-057 (`Confirmed`) has US pre-checked; page **502431750** (Login & Customer Account Workshop, 24 Sept 2026, unresolved) records *"Today US is opted in by default. Question to have all opted out moving forward… Validate this with Legal."* AGENTS.md currently encodes the old REG-057 behaviour.

---

## 7. Answering each question directly

- **Is there a real Emarsys front-end spec?** No. Nothing anywhere in the SFCC space specifies Emarsys front-end tracking. The TSD states positively that Emarsys has `No PWA involvement`; the reconciliation doc records `— (no PWA item)` / `Not Required`.
- **Is Emarsys Web Extend confirmed, deferred, or under investigation?** **Under investigation, unadjudicated.** Page 385318913's Status cell is blank and its Notes say `Tash to investigate (following previous conversation with TNL)`. Page 309690396 marks it `Emarsys (TBC)`. Jira SFCC-857 is `To Do` under the Enhancements epic. It is not approved against enhancement capacity, and it is not deferred either.
- **Who builds what?** Didomi PWA-side: **Accenture** (REG-048→056, all `Confirmed`) — limited to loading the SDK and respecting the signal. Didomi console/banner/regional defaults: **Didomi + Tell No Lies + Zimmermann**. GTM-housed tags: **Tell No Lies**. Emarsys front-end: **nobody is named, anywhere.** Tryzens appears only against legacy Magento work and Global-e credentials.
- **Is Didomi gating required before third-party scripts load?** Yes — REG-049, 303890433, TSD §11.1, plus fail-closed. Unambiguous, with the AAB-003 wrinkle in §6.1.
- **Does any Didomi implementation/design exist?** No. No Confluence page is titled for it; 299433985 is explicitly business-only with zero children; TSD §11 is policy-only with 8/9 IDs TBC; SFCC-107 is To Do; SFCC-106 is Blocked; `overrides/` has no Didomi code. The only implementation on record is Tryzens' script on the outgoing Magento platform.
- **Effort estimates found anywhere?** Only on page 385318913, and only for SFCC-857 (10 days total: BA 1 / FED 3 / BED 3 / Testing 3). **No consent or Didomi work carries any estimate on any page.** No story points appear anywhere in Confluence.

### Not chased
Attachment `att322535429` (`Updated Solution Architecture.pptx`) matched a loose "Web Extend" token search. **Inference:** almost certainly a false positive from separate "Web"/"Extend" tokens in extracted slide text, given "Scarab" returns zero everywhere. Not opened. Page **483131401** (TSD-SFCC-149/183, PDP Notify Me back-in-stock email trigger) is Emarsys-adjacent and real, but its documented decision is *"Back-in-stock emails must be sent from SFCC, not Emarsys"* — so it argues against, not for, Emarsys front-end scope.</result>

2. **04.1.17 (303890433) is stale on Optimizely and Crazy Egg** — it calls both GTM/AddingWell-managed and out of scope for SFCC. 4. **US marketing opt-in default is being reopened.** REG-057 (`Confirmed`) has US pre-checked; page **502431750** (Login & Customer Account Workshop, 24 Sept 2026, unresolved) records *"Today US is opted in by default. ## 7. Answering each question directly

- **Is there a real Emarsys front-end spec?** No. Nothing anywhere in the SFCC space specifies Emarsys front-end tracking. The TSD states positively that Emarsys has `No PWA involvement`; the reconciliation doc records `— (no PWA item)` / `Not Required`.
- **Is Emarsys Web Extend confirmed, deferred, or under investigation?** **Under investigation, unadjudicated.** Page 385318913's Status cell is blank and its Notes say `Tash to investigate (following previous conversation with TNL)`. Page 309690396 marks it `Emarsys (TBC)`. Jira SFCC-857 is `To Do` under the Enhancements epic. It is not approved against enhancement capacity, and it is not deferred either.
- **Who builds what?** Didomi PWA-side: **Accenture** (REG-048→056, all `Confirmed`) — limited to loading the SDK and respecting the signal. Didomi console/banner/regional defaults: **Didomi + Tell No Lies + Zimmermann**. GTM-housed tags: **Tell No Lies**. Emarsys front-end: **nobody is named, anywhere.** Tryzens appears only against legacy Magento work and Global-e credentials.
- **Is Didomi gating required before third-party scripts load?** Yes — REG-049, 303890433, TSD §11.1, plus fail-closed. Unambiguous, with the AAB-003 wrinkle in §6.1.
- **Does any Didomi implementation/design exist?** No. No Confluence page is titled for it; 299433985 is explicitly business-only with zero children; TSD §11 is policy-only with 8/9 IDs TBC; SFCC-107 is To Do; SFCC-106 is Blocked; `overrides/` has no Didomi code. The only implementation on record is Tryzens' script on the outgoing Magento platform.
- **Effort estimates found anywhere?** Only on page 385318913, and only for SFCC-857 (10 days total: BA 1 / FED 3 / BED 3 / Testing 3). **No consent or Didomi work carries any estimate on any page.** No story points appear anywhere in Confluence.

Attachment `att322535429` (`Updated Solution Architecture.pptx`) matched a loose "Web Extend" token search. **Inference:** almost certainly a false positive from separate "Web"/"Extend" tokens in extracted slide text, given "Scarab" returns zero everywhere. Not opened. ## 1. Confluence page 385318913 — "9.2 Enhancements"

**Table columns (6):** `Enhancement | Epic Mapping | Sizing | Status | Related User Story | Notes`

**~37 rows** (36 Jira-keyed + one free-text row "Data Anonymisation?? (Emma/Jas)").

### The three rows, verbatim

**SFCC-866**
| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Epic Mapping | `Cart` |
| Sizing | `BA - 0.5 day  FED - 2 days  Testing - 2 days` |
| Status | `Pending prioritisation` |

**SFCC-804**

**SFCC-950**
| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Epic Mapping | `Credit Notes & Gift Cards` |
| Sizing | `BA - 2 days  FED - 3 days  BED - 1 day  Testing - 3 days` |
| Status | **(empty)** |

| Notes | `Design - available  @Rebecca Jourdan to check how many online VICs / Gold Legacy that we have (will check with Steven)  Confirmed by @Rebecca Jourdan that there are no legacy gold VICs in our Intl sites. Retail rewards does not need to be in scope.  Pegged for future phase.` |

**Note:** the "Design - available" and "Double check if in designs" strings are in this **Confluence table's Notes column**, not in Jira. All three Jira issues have **zero comments**.

### There is no legend and no definition of "FED"
No glossary, no definition of BA/FED/BED/QA/Testing, no statement of what a "day" contains. The only quantitative basis is the **Enhancement Capacity** section: *"We have 2 sprints of Enhancements capacity, equivalent to 20 business days. With four disciplines involved — 1 x BA, 1 x FED, 1 x BED, and 1 x Testing — this gives us a combined total of 80 business days."* So "FED" = one front-end developer's elapsed business days, with no ideal-days/overhead definition.

### Yes — clearly entered per-row by different people at different times
Six independent tells:
1. **Punctuation split by block.** Rows SFCC-155→SFCC-184 use colons (`BA: 0.5 days`); rows SFCC-724→SFCC-950 use dashes (`BA - 2 days`).
2. **Discipline granularity changes.** Early rows combine `FED + BED: 4 days`; later rows split `FED - 3 days  BED - 1 day`.
3. **Label drift.** `QA:` (early) → `Testing:` (SFCC-174/173, transitional) → `Testing -` (late).
4. **Names instead of numbers** in estimate cells: SFCC-704 `BED: @Victor T. Crisostomo - need to determine where it's stored`; SFCC-724 `BED - @Victor T. Crisostomo  Testing - @Krizel B. Bartolome @Joseph Molina`.
5. **Data-entry error:** SFCC-683 has `BA: 0.5` sitting in the **Status** column, not Sizing.
6. **Unit inconsistency:** `0.5 day` vs `0.5 days`.

There is **no estimator/owner column** — nothing records who produced any figure.

### Do the three stand out? No — and that's the problem
FED values across the whole table cluster on just **2, 3, 5** (plus combined 2/4/5/7). That is coarse t-shirt sizing dressed as day estimates, not bottom-up estimation.

- **SFCC-866 (FED 2)** sits at the same value as SFCC-703 (PDP error template), SFCC-704 (PDP legal requirement, with design), SFCC-710 (whole PDP wishlist item). It is a single conditional branch on an action SFCC-272 already builds — materially smaller than any of those peers.
- **Testing is internally inconsistent:** SFCC-710 (a whole wishlist feature) got `Testing: 0.5 days`; SFCC-866 (one branch) got `Testing - 2 days`. 4× the QA for a fraction of the work.
- **SFCC-804 (FED 2)** and **SFCC-950 (FED 3)** are mid-pack, so nothing flags them — despite both being unsolved (below).

### Budget arithmetic — the headline
The capacity table shows **FED: 12.5 consumed, 7.5 remaining** (of 20).

- The three tickets total **FED 7 days = 93% of all remaining FED capacity.**
- Worse: rows already marked **Approved** but *not* in the consumed table — SFCC-135 (`FED + BED: 7 days`, ~3.5 FED), SFCC-724 (`FED - 5 days`), SFCC-859 (`FED - 5 days`), SFCC-946 (`FED - 2 days`) — add **~15.5 FED days against 7.5 remaining**. FED is roughly **2× oversubscribed before these three are even considered.**
- **Internal inconsistency:** SFCC-142's main row says `FED + BED: 5 days  QA: 3 days`; the consumed table records `FED 3.5 + DEV 3.5 = 7` and `QA 2`. The two tables disagree.

## 2. Spec pages found in space SFCC

### Global-E / international checkout / cart handoff — **real, detailed spec**
- **302612483 — 04.1.12 Price, Currency and Promotions** (`PRC` req prefix). The substantive one. **PRC-43** (Confirmed): cart handoff sends *"all applied promotions and coupon codes, **retail rewards**, gift cards"*. **PRC-16** (Confirmed): same, *"promotions, **rewards**, gift card redemptions"*. **PRC-46/PRC-53** carry explicit *"Open question"* comments on coupon and gift-card support.
- **303267844 — 04.1.7 Payments** (`PAY`). PAY-009, PAY-053, PAY-054 cover the redirect model.
- **330235905 — Global-E — Open Questions for SFCC / PWA Design.** Only 3 real questions; **all Response cells empty**.
- Supporting: 303398913 (04.1.2 Checkout Flow & Delivery), 303104002 (04.1.6 Regional Storefronts), 331218950 (15-07-2026 Global-e Meeting Notes — Send Cart hook, 1-page iframe), 431325185 (Global-e Configuration Reference), 362610693 (SFCC-131 Global-e & AvaTax Gap Analysis), 413925387 (TSD-SFCC-421), 292388871 (TSD: Price — Pricebooks & Global-e).

### VIP / VIC / loyalty / rewards / Omneo / AP21 — **real spec, but self-contradictory**
- **303267844 — 04.1.7 Payments**: PAY-027 → PAY-040 are a full Retail Rewards spec, **all scoped `US (domestic), AU (domestic), EU (domestic), UK (domestic)`**. AP21 balance validated in real time (PAY-031), rewards combinable with cards/GC/promos (PAY-027).
- **302612483 — PRC-45** (Confirmed, Accenture, Global-e markets, Custom): *"The system will support customer redemption of retail rewards at Global-e checkout for international markets. A maximum of one retail reward can be applied per order. Rewards are applied after promotions."* Comment: *"**Change in requirement comment**: Multiple retail rewards can be applied per order. For retail rewards - plan does not include third party retail rewards. We assume the rewards points are from AP21"*
- Also 302022672 (04.1.11 Customers/Account/CRM — Legacy VIC voucher display), 303890433 (04.1.17 Third Party Integrations), 407666693 (TSD: VIC Exclusive Product Visibility), 482345007 (04.4.6 VIC Exclusive Merchandiser Guide).

### Apple Pay / Google Pay / express checkout / Adyen — **real spec**
- **303267844**: **PAY-004** *"Apple Pay Express via Adyen in the mini bag on eligible devices"* (Custom, Confirmed); **PAY-006** Google Pay + Google Pay Express (Confirmed, *"currently targeting August 2026"*); **PAY-015** express-pay address validation occurs **post-authorisation**, rejected at Adyen level.
- 340000846 (9. Payment Configuration), 257228803 (Checkout — Adyen Drop-In architecture).

### Marketing opt-in / newsletter / consent / Emarsys — **real spec**
- **303104002 — 04.1.6 Regional Storefronts**: **REG-057** (Confirmed, Accenture, ALL, Custom): *"The system will display a marketing opt-in checkbox at **two points: on the guest checkout entry page and on the account registration page**. The checkbox will be unchecked by default for all storefronts except US, where it will be pre-checked."* **REG-058**: preference passed to Omneo on order placement (guests) / at registration (registered); *"Omneo will sync the preference to Emarsys."* REG-048→056 cover Didomi.
- **342360068 — 04.0 Requirements Workshops**: rows for **`2026-09-24 | Customer Account & CRM Workshop - Registration & Marketing Opt-in | Sprint 6`** and **`2026-09-28 | ... Marketing Opt-in 2`** and **`2026-09-28 | ... Loyalty & Rewards`**. The requirements underpinning SFCC-804 and SFCC-950 are **literally being workshopped today and this week**.
- **502431750 — Login & Customer Account Workshop (24 Sept 2026)**: *"Where does marketing opt-in get captured for social login registrations? Apple and Google don't surface it during their sign-in flow."* — the same unsolved shape as SFCC-804, still open.

### Wishlist — **real spec, but the SFCC-866 edge case is absent**
- **302415874 — 04.1.5 Cart and Inventory**: *"display a Move to Wishlist and Remove action per line item in the mini-cart"*; *"allow customers to remove an item or move it to their wishlist from the cart page"*. **No requirement anywhere covers the already-in-wishlist collision.**
- 302022672 (04.1.11 — wishlist add/notification banner), 303693825 (04.1.13 — MOVE TO WISHLIST on gift card lines).

## 3. Design + agreed solution, per ticket

Primary source: **258801666 — 04.2 Design Tracker** (has the Figma links; single Figma file `XWz3ItpkSqL45P5IFOnQgB` "Design Workspace") and **408944644 — 04.72 Component Design & User Story Tracker**. These two disagree; 04.2's own preamble and all its dated comments are June/July, so treat 04.72 as the live one and 04.2 as indicative of status/gaps.

**SFCC-866 — design: partial. Agreed solution: yes (in the Jira description).**
The 04.2 Cart & Inventory rows cover **Mini-Cart** (`move-to-wishlist/remove`) and **Full Cart Page** (incl. named error states: OOS notification, max-3-units error) — both **Design Status PENDING / Zimmermann Sign-off Pending**. 04.72 says Cart components were finalised **Aug 24 (Sprint 3)**. Either way, **the "item already in wishlist" state is not itemised anywhere in either tracker**, even though sibling cart error states are. So the Kiera Rikard-Bell check resolves to: *the action is designed, the collision case is not.* Note 04.72's hard rule — *"Once a component is finalised and added to the UI kit, it is locked... Any change after lock requires a formal review of every story and epic that references that component."*
The solution itself *is* agreed — SFCC-866's description is unambiguous and self-contained, and confirms *"This requires custom PWA Kit development — it is not achievable with SFCC OOTB behaviour."*

**SFCC-804 — design: none. Agreed solution: explicitly none.**
The ticket says so itself: **"This story is currently a placeholder — no solution has been agreed. Requires input from Emma/Rebecca (business requirements), Keira (UX design), and Tim (technical feasibility) before ACs can be written."** It also flags *"implications for GDPR/privacy compliance... legal sign-off may be required."*
Corroborated by the Design Tracker: the **Payments** row's scope includes *"Apple Pay / Google Pay express in mini-bag"* but **contains no marketing opt-in at all** — status **PENDING / Pending**, with an open Accenture note *"**23-06**: is mini bag still in progress (Apple Pay/Google Pay express)?"*. The only marketing-opt-in design entries anywhere are under *Checkout Flow & Delivery → Order Review & Confirmation* and *Customer Account & CRM → Login and Registration* — both PENDING, neither express-checkout. **An estimate of BA 1 + Design 0.5 + FED 2 + BED 2 + Testing 2 has been placed on a story that states its own ACs cannot yet be written.**

**SFCC-950 — "Design - available" is not supported by the trackers.**
- SFCC-950 is mapped to the **Credit Notes & Gift Cards** epic. That epic's 04.2 row is **PENDING / Pending** and its component detail is entirely GiveX gift-card content — **no VIP/Retail Rewards and no Global-E content whatsoever**.
- The nearest real artefact is the **Payments** row: *"**17-06:** Shared saved cards selection & Retail Rewards with design team"* — i.e. *briefed to* design, not delivered; row is **PENDING / Pending**. 04.72 lists *"retail rewards redemption"* under Payments with components finalised **Sep 7 (Sprint 4)** — but that is the **Zimmermann-owned domestic payment step**, which PAY-027 scopes to domestic storefronts only.
- Structurally, **Global-E owns the international checkout UI** (1-page iframe, per 331218950 and REG-007/008). A Zimmermann Figma design for redemption *inside* that iframe is not something the design tracker could plausibly hold.

**Verdict: "Design - available" most likely refers to the domestic Retail Rewards payment-step design and has been misapplied to the Global-E variant.**

### Three further blockers on SFCC-950 that the 9-day estimate does not reflect
1. **Feasibility is an open, unanswered question.** 330235905 Q2, raised by Jasmijn, Priority Medium: *"Confirm whether global-e can support AP21 retail rewards redemption in international checkouts - **limitation today**"* — **Response column empty.**
2. **The ticket's own description is a Global-E reply written about the legacy Magento site:** *"Zimmermann will need to modify the implementation to pass the points and value from the **Magento cart** to our checkout via API for us to support this feature. **We cannot integrate with AP21** as the Zimmermann checkout does today. Currently available in domestic checkout. Not available in international checkout."* It is stale w.r.t. SFCC and makes the work a cart-handoff payload change plus a Global-E-side capability, not a UI build.
3. **Two Confirmed requirements directly contradict each other:**
 - **PRC-45** (Confirmed): *"will support customer redemption of retail rewards at Global-e checkout for international markets."*
 - **PAY-039** (Confirmed): *"will display messaging in My Account for customers on Global-e-operated storefronts (HK, ME, EU International) directing VIP clients to contact Client Services to redeem Retail Rewards, **as online redemption is not supported on these storefronts**."*
 Both came from the same signed-off July 3rd requirements extract.

**And the enhancement table's own note kills it anyway:** *"Confirmed by @Rebecca Jourdan that there are no legacy gold VICs in our Intl sites. **Retail rewards does not need to be in scope.** Pegged for future phase."* — yet the row still carries 9 days total.

**Double-count risk:** because PRC-16, PRC-43 and PRC-45 are **Confirmed baseline requirements owned by Accenture**, SFCC-950 is either already inside the baseline estimate or the baseline was never costed for it. It should not be a separate 9-day enhancement draw without resolving that.

---

## 4. Dependency tickets — all four exist

| Key | Summary | Status | Assignee | Updated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-272** | Cart Item - Remove and Wishlist Actions | **In Progress** | Marcel Angelo Navarro | 2026-09-24 |
| **SFCC-325** | Cart Page – Newsletter Sign Up Component | **To Do** | Tim Lavelle | 2026-08-25 |
| **SFCC-383** | Payments – Apple Pay Express Button (Cart Page & Mini Bag) | **To Do** | Unassigned | 2026-09-09 |
| **SFCC-384** | Payments – Google Pay Express Button (Cart Page & Mini Bag) | **To Do** | Unassigned | 2026-09-09 |

None are Done. **All three of SFCC-804's named dependencies are To Do and two are unassigned** — so the express-checkout surface it needs to hook into does not exist yet.

**Naming mismatch worth flagging:** SFCC-804's description cites *"SFCC-325 (Cart Page – **Marketing Opt-In Checkbox**)"*, but SFCC-325's actual title is *"Cart Page – **Newsletter Sign Up** Component"*. Separately, **REG-057 does not specify a cart-page opt-in at all** — it names only the guest checkout entry page and the account registration page. SFCC-804's entire gap premise ("the standard cart page includes a marketing opt-in checkbox") rests on a requirement that isn't in the signed-off set.

### The three enhancement tickets themselves
| Key | Summary | Status | Priority | Comments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC-866 | Enhancement – Auto-Remove Cart Item When Moving to Wishlist if Item Already Exists in Wishlist | To Do | **Low** | 0 |
| SFCC-804 | Enhancement – Marketing Opt-In Capture for Apple Pay & Google Pay Express Checkout Customers | To Do | Medium | 0 |
| SFCC-950 | VIP Rewards Redemption at Checkout via Global-E | To Do | Medium | 0 |

All three parent to epic **SFCC-24 (Enhancements)**. SFCC-950 returned no `labels` — the 9.2 page's dashboard link filters on `labels = MustHave`, so it may not appear on the dashboard the page points readers to.

---

### Bottom line for the audit
- **SFCC-866** — the only one of the three with an agreed solution. FED 2 is generous for one conditional branch on work SFCC-272 is already building, and its Testing 2 is 4× what a larger wishlist item (SFCC-710) got. Real dependency risk is low; SFCC-272 is in progress.
- **SFCC-804** — FED 2 (and 7.5 days total) estimated against a story that states no solution is agreed, no ACs can be written, no design exists, all three dependencies are To Do, and the requirement it's premised on (cart-page opt-in) isn't in the signed-off REG set. This is an unestimatable placeholder with a number attached.
- **SFCC-950** — FED 3 (9 days total) on work that is (a) already Confirmed baseline scope under PRC-16/43/45, (b) contradicted by Confirmed PAY-039, (c) gated on an unanswered Global-E feasibility question flagged as a "limitation today", (d) described by a stale Magento-era Global-E quote, and (e) declared out of scope by the table's own note. The "Design - available" claim does not survive checking.
- **Process-level:** FED capacity is already ~2× oversubscribed by approved-but-unconsumed rows before these three (which would consume 93% of nominal remaining FED). No estimator is recorded anywhere, no discipline is defined, and the two capacity tables disagree on SFCC-142.

*(All Confluence and Jira access was read-only. No pages, issues, or comments were created or modified.)*</result>
