<result>I have what I need. Writing up the findings.

## 1. Confluence page 385318913 — "9.2 Enhancements"

**Table columns (6):** `Enhancement | Epic Mapping | Sizing | Status | Related User Story | Notes`

**~37 rows** (36 Jira-keyed + one free-text row "Data Anonymisation?? (Emma/Jas)").

### The three rows, verbatim

**SFCC-866**
| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Epic Mapping | `Cart` |
| Sizing | `BA - 0.5 day  FED - 2 days  Testing - 2 days` |
| Status | `Pending prioritisation` |
| Related User Story | *(empty)* |
| Notes | `Raised as low  Double check if in designs @Kiera Rikard-Bell  BED - None needed. We have existing APIs for this already` |

**SFCC-804**
| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Epic Mapping | `Payments` |
| Sizing | `BA - 1 day  Design - 0.5 day  FED - 2 days  BED - 2 days  Testing - 2 days` |
| Status | **(empty)** |
| Related User Story | *(empty)* |
| Notes | `Under shipping and on top of payments  Deferred to Phase 2` |

**SFCC-950**
| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Epic Mapping | `Credit Notes & Gift Cards` |
| Sizing | `BA - 2 days  FED - 3 days  BED - 1 day  Testing - 3 days` |
| Status | **(empty)** |
| Related User Story | *(empty)* |
| Notes | `Design - available  @Rebecca Jourdan to check how many online VICs / Gold Legacy that we have (will check with Steven)  Confirmed by @Rebecca Jourdan that there are no legacy gold VICs in our Intl sites. Retail rewards does not need to be in scope.  Pegged for future phase.` |

**Note:** the "Design - available" and "Double check if in designs" strings are in this **Confluence table's Notes column**, not in Jira. All three Jira issues have **zero comments**.

### There is no legend and no definition of "FED"
No glossary, no definition of BA/FED/BED/QA/Testing, no statement of what a "day" contains. The only quantitative basis is the **Enhancement Capacity** section: *"We have 2 sprints of Enhancements capacity, equivalent to 20 business days. With four disciplines involved — 1 x BA, 1 x FED, 1 x BED, and 1 x Testing — this gives us a combined total of 80 business days."* So "FED" = one front-end developer's elapsed business days, with no ideal-days/overhead definition.

### Yes — clearly entered per-row by different people at different times
Six independent tells:
1. **Punctuation split by block.** Rows SFCC-155→SFCC-184 use colons (`BA: 0.5 days`); rows SFCC-724→SFCC-950 use dashes (`BA - 2 days`).
2. **Discipline granularity changes.** Early rows combine `FED + BED: 4 days`; later rows split `FED - 3 days  BED - 1 day`.
3. **Label drift.** `QA:` (early) → `Testing:` (SFCC-174/173, transitional) → `Testing -` (late).
4. **Names instead of numbers** in estimate cells: SFCC-704 `BED: @Victor T. Crisostomo - need to determine where it's stored`; SFCC-724 `BED - @Victor T. Crisostomo  Testing - @Krizel B. Bartolome @Joseph Molina`.
5. **Data-entry error:** SFCC-683 has `BA: 0.5` sitting in the **Status** column, not Sizing.
6. **Unit inconsistency:** `0.5 day` vs `0.5 days`.

There is **no estimator/owner column** — nothing records who produced any figure.

### Do the three stand out? No — and that's the problem
FED values across the whole table cluster on just **2, 3, 5** (plus combined 2/4/5/7). That is coarse t-shirt sizing dressed as day estimates, not bottom-up estimation.

- **SFCC-866 (FED 2)** sits at the same value as SFCC-703 (PDP error template), SFCC-704 (PDP legal requirement, with design), SFCC-710 (whole PDP wishlist item). It is a single conditional branch on an action SFCC-272 already builds — materially smaller than any of those peers.
- **Testing is internally inconsistent:** SFCC-710 (a whole wishlist feature) got `Testing: 0.5 days`; SFCC-866 (one branch) got `Testing - 2 days`. 4× the QA for a fraction of the work.
- **SFCC-804 (FED 2)** and **SFCC-950 (FED 3)** are mid-pack, so nothing flags them — despite both being unsolved (below).

### Budget arithmetic — the headline
The capacity table shows **FED: 12.5 consumed, 7.5 remaining** (of 20).

- The three tickets total **FED 7 days = 93% of all remaining FED capacity.**
- Worse: rows already marked **Approved** but *not* in the consumed table — SFCC-135 (`FED + BED: 7 days`, ~3.5 FED), SFCC-724 (`FED - 5 days`), SFCC-859 (`FED - 5 days`), SFCC-946 (`FED - 2 days`) — add **~15.5 FED days against 7.5 remaining**. FED is roughly **2× oversubscribed before these three are even considered.**
- **Internal inconsistency:** SFCC-142's main row says `FED + BED: 5 days  QA: 3 days`; the consumed table records `FED 3.5 + DEV 3.5 = 7` and `QA 2`. The two tables disagree.

---

## 2. Spec pages found in space SFCC

### Global-E / international checkout / cart handoff — **real, detailed spec**
- **302612483 — 04.1.12 Price, Currency and Promotions** (`PRC` req prefix). The substantive one. **PRC-43** (Confirmed): cart handoff sends *"all applied promotions and coupon codes, **retail rewards**, gift cards"*. **PRC-16** (Confirmed): same, *"promotions, **rewards**, gift card redemptions"*. **PRC-46/PRC-53** carry explicit *"Open question"* comments on coupon and gift-card support.
- **303267844 — 04.1.7 Payments** (`PAY`). PAY-009, PAY-053, PAY-054 cover the redirect model.
- **330235905 — Global-E — Open Questions for SFCC / PWA Design.** Only 3 real questions; **all Response cells empty**.
- Supporting: 303398913 (04.1.2 Checkout Flow & Delivery), 303104002 (04.1.6 Regional Storefronts), 331218950 (15-07-2026 Global-e Meeting Notes — Send Cart hook, 1-page iframe), 431325185 (Global-e Configuration Reference), 362610693 (SFCC-131 Global-e & AvaTax Gap Analysis), 413925387 (TSD-SFCC-421), 292388871 (TSD: Price — Pricebooks & Global-e).

### VIP / VIC / loyalty / rewards / Omneo / AP21 — **real spec, but self-contradictory**
- **303267844 — 04.1.7 Payments**: PAY-027 → PAY-040 are a full Retail Rewards spec, **all scoped `US (domestic), AU (domestic), EU (domestic), UK (domestic)`**. AP21 balance validated in real time (PAY-031), rewards combinable with cards/GC/promos (PAY-027).
- **302612483 — PRC-45** (Confirmed, Accenture, Global-e markets, Custom): *"The system will support customer redemption of retail rewards at Global-e checkout for international markets. A maximum of one retail reward can be applied per order. Rewards are applied after promotions."* Comment: *"**Change in requirement comment**: Multiple retail rewards can be applied per order. For retail rewards - plan does not include third party retail rewards. We assume the rewards points are from AP21"*
- Also 302022672 (04.1.11 Customers/Account/CRM — Legacy VIC voucher display), 303890433 (04.1.17 Third Party Integrations), 407666693 (TSD: VIC Exclusive Product Visibility), 482345007 (04.4.6 VIC Exclusive Merchandiser Guide).

### Apple Pay / Google Pay / express checkout / Adyen — **real spec**
- **303267844**: **PAY-004** *"Apple Pay Express via Adyen in the mini bag on eligible devices"* (Custom, Confirmed); **PAY-006** Google Pay + Google Pay Express (Confirmed, *"currently targeting August 2026"*); **PAY-015** express-pay address validation occurs **post-authorisation**, rejected at Adyen level.
- 340000846 (9. Payment Configuration), 257228803 (Checkout — Adyen Drop-In architecture).

### Marketing opt-in / newsletter / consent / Emarsys — **real spec**
- **303104002 — 04.1.6 Regional Storefronts**: **REG-057** (Confirmed, Accenture, ALL, Custom): *"The system will display a marketing opt-in checkbox at **two points: on the guest checkout entry page and on the account registration page**. The checkbox will be unchecked by default for all storefronts except US, where it will be pre-checked."* **REG-058**: preference passed to Omneo on order placement (guests) / at registration (registered); *"Omneo will sync the preference to Emarsys."* REG-048→056 cover Didomi.
- **342360068 — 04.0 Requirements Workshops**: rows for **`2026-09-24 | Customer Account & CRM Workshop - Registration & Marketing Opt-in | Sprint 6`** and **`2026-09-28 | ... Marketing Opt-in 2`** and **`2026-09-28 | ... Loyalty & Rewards`**. The requirements underpinning SFCC-804 and SFCC-950 are **literally being workshopped today and this week**.
- **502431750 — Login & Customer Account Workshop (24 Sept 2026)**: *"Where does marketing opt-in get captured for social login registrations? Apple and Google don't surface it during their sign-in flow."* — the same unsolved shape as SFCC-804, still open.

### Wishlist — **real spec, but the SFCC-866 edge case is absent**
- **302415874 — 04.1.5 Cart and Inventory**: *"display a Move to Wishlist and Remove action per line item in the mini-cart"*; *"allow customers to remove an item or move it to their wishlist from the cart page"*. **No requirement anywhere covers the already-in-wishlist collision.**
- 302022672 (04.1.11 — wishlist add/notification banner), 303693825 (04.1.13 — MOVE TO WISHLIST on gift card lines).

---

## 3. Design + agreed solution, per ticket

Primary source: **258801666 — 04.2 Design Tracker** (has the Figma links; single Figma file `XWz3ItpkSqL45P5IFOnQgB` "Design Workspace") and **408944644 — 04.72 Component Design & User Story Tracker**. These two disagree; 04.2's own preamble and all its dated comments are June/July, so treat 04.72 as the live one and 04.2 as indicative of status/gaps.

**SFCC-866 — design: partial. Agreed solution: yes (in the Jira description).**
The 04.2 Cart & Inventory rows cover **Mini-Cart** (`move-to-wishlist/remove`) and **Full Cart Page** (incl. named error states: OOS notification, max-3-units error) — both **Design Status PENDING / Zimmermann Sign-off Pending**. 04.72 says Cart components were finalised **Aug 24 (Sprint 3)**. Either way, **the "item already in wishlist" state is not itemised anywhere in either tracker**, even though sibling cart error states are. So the Kiera Rikard-Bell check resolves to: *the action is designed, the collision case is not.* Note 04.72's hard rule — *"Once a component is finalised and added to the UI kit, it is locked... Any change after lock requires a formal review of every story and epic that references that component."*
The solution itself *is* agreed — SFCC-866's description is unambiguous and self-contained, and confirms *"This requires custom PWA Kit development — it is not achievable with SFCC OOTB behaviour."*

**SFCC-804 — design: none. Agreed solution: explicitly none.**
The ticket says so itself: **"This story is currently a placeholder — no solution has been agreed. Requires input from Emma/Rebecca (business requirements), Keira (UX design), and Tim (technical feasibility) before ACs can be written."** It also flags *"implications for GDPR/privacy compliance... legal sign-off may be required."*
Corroborated by the Design Tracker: the **Payments** row's scope includes *"Apple Pay / Google Pay express in mini-bag"* but **contains no marketing opt-in at all** — status **PENDING / Pending**, with an open Accenture note *"**23-06**: is mini bag still in progress (Apple Pay/Google Pay express)?"*. The only marketing-opt-in design entries anywhere are under *Checkout Flow & Delivery → Order Review & Confirmation* and *Customer Account & CRM → Login and Registration* — both PENDING, neither express-checkout. **An estimate of BA 1 + Design 0.5 + FED 2 + BED 2 + Testing 2 has been placed on a story that states its own ACs cannot yet be written.**

**SFCC-950 — "Design - available" is not supported by the trackers.**
- SFCC-950 is mapped to the **Credit Notes & Gift Cards** epic. That epic's 04.2 row is **PENDING / Pending** and its component detail is entirely GiveX gift-card content — **no VIP/Retail Rewards and no Global-E content whatsoever**.
- The nearest real artefact is the **Payments** row: *"**17-06:** Shared saved cards selection & Retail Rewards with design team"* — i.e. *briefed to* design, not delivered; row is **PENDING / Pending**. 04.72 lists *"retail rewards redemption"* under Payments with components finalised **Sep 7 (Sprint 4)** — but that is the **Zimmermann-owned domestic payment step**, which PAY-027 scopes to domestic storefronts only.
- Structurally, **Global-E owns the international checkout UI** (1-page iframe, per 331218950 and REG-007/008). A Zimmermann Figma design for redemption *inside* that iframe is not something the design tracker could plausibly hold.

**Verdict: "Design - available" most likely refers to the domestic Retail Rewards payment-step design and has been misapplied to the Global-E variant.**

### Three further blockers on SFCC-950 that the 9-day estimate does not reflect
1. **Feasibility is an open, unanswered question.** 330235905 Q2, raised by Jasmijn, Priority Medium: *"Confirm whether global-e can support AP21 retail rewards redemption in international checkouts - **limitation today**"* — **Response column empty.**
2. **The ticket's own description is a Global-E reply written about the legacy Magento site:** *"Zimmermann will need to modify the implementation to pass the points and value from the **Magento cart** to our checkout via API for us to support this feature. **We cannot integrate with AP21** as the Zimmermann checkout does today. Currently available in domestic checkout. Not available in international checkout."* It is stale w.r.t. SFCC and makes the work a cart-handoff payload change plus a Global-E-side capability, not a UI build.
3. **Two Confirmed requirements directly contradict each other:**
 - **PRC-45** (Confirmed): *"will support customer redemption of retail rewards at Global-e checkout for international markets."*
 - **PAY-039** (Confirmed): *"will display messaging in My Account for customers on Global-e-operated storefronts (HK, ME, EU International) directing VIP clients to contact Client Services to redeem Retail Rewards, **as online redemption is not supported on these storefronts**."*
 Both came from the same signed-off July 3rd requirements extract.

**And the enhancement table's own note kills it anyway:** *"Confirmed by @Rebecca Jourdan that there are no legacy gold VICs in our Intl sites. **Retail rewards does not need to be in scope.** Pegged for future phase."* — yet the row still carries 9 days total.

**Double-count risk:** because PRC-16, PRC-43 and PRC-45 are **Confirmed baseline requirements owned by Accenture**, SFCC-950 is either already inside the baseline estimate or the baseline was never costed for it. It should not be a separate 9-day enhancement draw without resolving that.

---

## 4. Dependency tickets — all four exist

| Key | Summary | Status | Assignee | Updated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-272** | Cart Item - Remove and Wishlist Actions | **In Progress** | Marcel Angelo Navarro | 2026-09-24 |
| **SFCC-325** | Cart Page – Newsletter Sign Up Component | **To Do** | Tim Lavelle | 2026-08-25 |
| **SFCC-383** | Payments – Apple Pay Express Button (Cart Page & Mini Bag) | **To Do** | Unassigned | 2026-09-09 |
| **SFCC-384** | Payments – Google Pay Express Button (Cart Page & Mini Bag) | **To Do** | Unassigned | 2026-09-09 |

None are Done. **All three of SFCC-804's named dependencies are To Do and two are unassigned** — so the express-checkout surface it needs to hook into does not exist yet.

**Naming mismatch worth flagging:** SFCC-804's description cites *"SFCC-325 (Cart Page – **Marketing Opt-In Checkbox**)"*, but SFCC-325's actual title is *"Cart Page – **Newsletter Sign Up** Component"*. Separately, **REG-057 does not specify a cart-page opt-in at all** — it names only the guest checkout entry page and the account registration page. SFCC-804's entire gap premise ("the standard cart page includes a marketing opt-in checkbox") rests on a requirement that isn't in the signed-off set.

### The three enhancement tickets themselves
| Key | Summary | Status | Priority | Comments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC-866 | Enhancement – Auto-Remove Cart Item When Moving to Wishlist if Item Already Exists in Wishlist | To Do | **Low** | 0 |
| SFCC-804 | Enhancement – Marketing Opt-In Capture for Apple Pay & Google Pay Express Checkout Customers | To Do | Medium | 0 |
| SFCC-950 | VIP Rewards Redemption at Checkout via Global-E | To Do | Medium | 0 |

All three parent to epic **SFCC-24 (Enhancements)**. SFCC-950 returned no `labels` — the 9.2 page's dashboard link filters on `labels = MustHave`, so it may not appear on the dashboard the page points readers to.

content.text:
Audit closed. Late agents got Confluence to load, so my main verification gap is now shut: **every figure in the capacity analysis is independently re-verified against v17**, and the page has no comments hiding anything.

Three things landed after the version I sent earlier.

## Nobody knows who produced these numbers

There's no estimator column, no legend, no definition of BA/FED/BED/QA. And the rows were clearly entered by different people at different times — punctuation splits the table in half (colons up to SFCC-184, dashes from SFCC-724), the QA label drifts `QA:` → `Testing:` → `Testing -`, two cells contain **names instead of numbers**, and SFCC-683's `BA: 0.5` is sitting in the **Status** column.

FED values cluster on just 2, 3 and 5. That's t-shirt sizing presented as days. The QA column proves it: **SFCC-710, an entire wishlist feature, got Testing 0.5 days. SFCC-866, one conditional branch, got Testing 2.** Four times the QA for a fraction of the work.

This is the real explanation for the whole pattern. A "2" meaning *smallish* and a "2" meaning *two days* sum differently, and the capacity table sums them as the second.

## SFCC-950 is a head-on collision between two Confirmed requirements

Both signed off in the same 3 July extract:

- **PRC-45** — *"will support customer redemption of retail rewards at Global-e checkout for international markets."*
- **PAY-039** — *"online redemption is **not supported** on these storefronts."*

And Global-E's own feasibility question — *"Confirm whether global-e can support AP21 retail rewards redemption… **limitation today**"* — has an empty Response cell. The ticket description is a stale Global-E reply about the *Magento* cart. It also has **no labels**, so it never appears on the MustHave dashboard the page cites as its source of truth.

## SFCC-804's premise isn't in the signed-off requirements

It claims the cart page has a marketing opt-in that express shoppers bypass. **REG-057 specifies two touchpoints — guest checkout entry and account registration. No cart page.** And the dependency it names as "SFCC-325 (Cart Page – Marketing Opt-In Checkbox)" is actually titled "Cart Page – **Newsletter Sign Up** Component".

## One thing worth five minutes

Page 268337165 records the Didomi Notice IDs as a *"Hard blocker — Didomi SDK cannot be configured without Notice IDs"*. Page 264765445 already contains the production Didomi loader with the SDK key and **11 per-storefront Notice IDs**. It's Tryzens' Magento-era work and nobody has checked whether the IDs still apply — but if they do, a blocker sitting under two estimates is partially self-answering.

---

Nothing written to Jira or Confluence. Final document above.

**What you're missing:** the requirements under SFCC-804 and SFCC-950 are being workshopped **today and this week** — 24 Sept Registration & Marketing Opt-in, 28 Sept Marketing Opt-in 2, 28 Sept Loyalty & Rewards. Both rows carry firm day-counts against requirements actively being rewritten in a room you can walk into. Two consequences you should decide on before Monday: the 24 Sept workshop is already asking whether the US marketing opt-in should flip from pre-checked to opted-out, and **AGENTS.md encodes the current REG-057 behaviour as a standing rule** — if that decision lands, that's a Tier 1 doc edit someone has to own, and it isn't automatic. The second is simpler: if Loyalty & Rewards on the 28th resolves the PRC-45 vs PAY-039 conflict, SFCC-950's 9 days either disappear or become real, and that's the single largest binary on the tracker. Getting those two questions onto those agendas costs you one message each and is worth more than any re-estimate in this document.

---

# A. Inside Chat / live chat / co-browsing

## The headline: co-browsing does not exist in Confluence

I ran CQL text searches across space SFCC for `co-browsing`, `cobrowse`, `co-browse`, and a title search for `Browsing`. **Zero pages contain any co-browsing content.** The three pages returned by the `co-browsing` CQL query (407666693 TSD VIC Exclusive Product Visibility, 304775192 Claude Code Onboarding, 264765445 Technical Files) are tokeniser false-positives — none mentions co-browsing, screen sharing, or session sharing.

There is also **no page titled with "Chat"** anywhere in the space. The "Client Services Persona" page (**248676356**) — the persona that owns SFCC-858's epic — describes their Magento tooling in detail and **never mentions Inside Chat, live chat, or co-browsing at all**.

**Nothing in Confluence states whether InsideChat supports co-browsing out of the box, and there is no vendor confirmation of any kind.** The only reference to the question is the open question in the 9.2 table itself (quoted below).

## Inside Chat is script-injection only, owned by Zimmermann, not built by the PWA team

The requirement is one line, from the confirmed functional requirements (**303890433**, "04.1.17 Third Party Integrations"):

> "The system will support Inside Chat live chat widget loading via GTM script injection through the AddingWell container. **Inside Chat configuration and routing logic are out of scope for SFCC and remain with Zimmermann.**"

Consistent across every source:
- **261849101** (1.4 Third Party Overview): "Live chat / support widget, **loaded via GTM post-consent**"
- **256933898** (Integration Overview) files it under "**Client Side Scripts managed via GTM/Addingwell, configured by Tell No Lies**" — Integration Type "Script Injection", Details "Manage through GTM". Open question: "How is InsideChat receives the customer information in the chat session."
- **299433985** (04.6 Consent Management): "Fully managed by Tell No Lies inside the GTM container. **Consent gating is Tell No Lies' responsibility — not in Accenture's scope**"

**Not implemented anywhere yet.** **307134467** (Integration Reconciliation) records Inside Chat as **INT-027, status "Under Review"**, and `projectState.md` status "Not started". **268337165** (7.1b Third Party Credentials) lists the Inside Chat row as "Required before Inside Chat widget can be tested" — i.e. credentials not yet held. **No storefront/region enablement list exists anywhere** — no page states which of the 8 storefronts Inside Chat is on.

## The only two hard front-end requirements (303071234, "04.1.1 Homepage and Content")

Both are Sub-Functional Area "Chat Integration", both **Status = Confirmed**, both with empty Comments:

| Req ID | Requirement | Status |
|---|---|---|
| HPC-039 *(Req ID cell renders blank; the row's Jira link is labelled `PRD-039`)* | "The system should display the chat widget as a pop-up overlay on the relevant pages. **Page visibility rules are determined by Inside Chat.**" | Confirmed |
| HPC-040 | "The system should only initialise the chat widget **after the customer has consented to the relevant cookie category via Didomi**." | Confirmed |

So the entire FE obligation is: let GTM inject it, and don't let it fire pre-consent. Page-visibility logic is explicitly the vendor's.

## Three open questions the integration register still carries

Per **307134467**: *"Confluence actually has 3 open questions (chat suppression rules, which attributes get passed, page scope) that openItems.md says don't exist. openItems.md is wrong here, not Confluence."* Their sources:

- **258441217** (Store Details, INT-027): "Live chat widget available on Store Detail page for click-and-collect queries and boutique appointment booking… Inside Chat JS SDK". Open question: *"Is Inside Chat shown on all Store pages or only when a shopper has a product in context (BOPIS flow)?"*
- **257163291** (My Account, INT-027): "customer identity automatically injected into chat context… Customer name, email, loyalty tier injected into chat widget". Open question: *"Confirm which customer attributes are passed to Inside Chat"*
- **256442388** (Order Details, INT-027): "passes customer identity and order ID as context to chat agent". Open question: *"Confirm chat suppression on checkout pages vs…"*

Note the **contradiction with HPC-039**: these three pages describe SFCC/PWA injecting customer identity, order ID and loyalty tier into the chat context, while 303890433 says routing/config is wholly out of SFCC scope and HPC-039 says visibility is vendor-controlled. Nobody has reconciled who does the identity injection.

# B. Avalara / tax calculation

# A. Inside Chat / live chat / co-browsing

## The headline: co-browsing does not exist in Confluence

I ran CQL text searches across space SFCC for `co-browsing`, `cobrowse`, `co-browse`, and a title search for `Browsing`. **Zero pages contain any co-browsing content.** The three pages returned by the `co-browsing` CQL query (407666693 TSD VIC Exclusive Product Visibility, 304775192 Claude Code Onboarding, 264765445 Technical Files) are tokeniser false-positives — none mentions co-browsing, screen sharing, or session sharing.

There is also **no page titled with "Chat"** anywhere in the space. The "Client Services Persona" page (**248676356**) — the persona that owns SFCC-858's epic — describes their Magento tooling in detail and **never mentions Inside Chat, live chat, or co-browsing at all**.

**Nothing in Confluence states whether InsideChat supports co-browsing out of the box, and there is no vendor confirmation of any kind.** The only reference to the question is the open question in the 9.2 table itself (quoted below).

- **256933898** (Integration Overview) files it under "**Client Side Scripts managed via GTM/Addingwell, configured by Tell No Lies**" — Integration Type "Script Injection", Details "Manage through GTM". Open question: "How is InsideChat receives the customer information in the chat session."
- **299433985** (04.6 Consent Management): "Fully managed by Tell No Lies inside the GTM container. **Consent gating is Tell No Lies' responsibility — not in Accenture's scope**"

**Not implemented anywhere yet.** **307134467** (Integration Reconciliation) records Inside Chat as **INT-027, status "Under Review"**, and `projectState.md` status "Not started". **268337165** (7.1b Third Party Credentials) lists the Inside Chat row as "Required before Inside Chat widget can be tested" — i.e. credentials not yet held. **No storefront/region enablement list exists anywhere** — no page states which of the 8 storefronts Inside Chat is on.

## The only two hard front-end requirements (303071234, "04.1.1 Homepage and Content")

Both are Sub-Functional Area "Chat Integration", both **Status = Confirmed**, both with empty Comments:

| Req ID | Requirement | Status |
|---|---|---|
| HPC-039 *(Req ID cell renders blank; the row's Jira link is labelled `PRD-039`)* | "The system should display the chat widget as a pop-up overlay on the relevant pages. **Page visibility rules are determined by Inside Chat.**" | Confirmed |
| HPC-040 | "The system should only initialise the chat widget **after the customer has consented to the relevant cookie category via Didomi**." | Confirmed |

So the entire FE obligation is: let GTM inject it, and don't let it fire pre-consent. Page-visibility logic is explicitly the vendor's.

## Three open questions the integration register still carries

Per **307134467**: *"Confluence actually has 3 open questions (chat suppression rules, which attributes get passed, page scope) that openItems.md says don't exist. openItems.md is wrong here, not Confluence."* Their sources:

- **258441217** (Store Details, INT-027): "Live chat widget available on Store Detail page for click-and-collect queries and boutique appointment booking… Inside Chat JS SDK". Open question: *"Is Inside Chat shown on all Store pages or only when a shopper has a product in context (BOPIS flow)?"*
- **257163291** (My Account, INT-027): "customer identity automatically injected into chat context… Customer name, email, loyalty tier injected into chat widget". Open question: *"Confirm which customer attributes are passed to Inside Chat"*
- **256442388** (Order Details, INT-027): "passes customer identity and order ID as context to chat agent". Open question: *"Confirm chat suppression on checkout pages vs…"*

Note the **contradiction with HPC-039**: these three pages describe SFCC/PWA injecting customer identity, order ID and loyalty tier into the chat context, while 303890433 says routing/config is wholly out of SFCC scope and HPC-039 says visibility is vendor-controlled. Nobody has reconciled who does the identity injection.

**All Atlassian access was read-only.** Nothing was written, commented, created, updated or transitioned.

## TASK 1 — Confluence page 385318913 "9.2 Enhancements"

Retrieved successfully (after 3 retries). Space: SFCC ("Adobe SFCC"). **Version 17.**

### 1a. The three rows, verbatim

Column order: *Enhancement | Epic Mapping | Sizing | Status | Related User Story | Notes*

**SFCC-174**
> | SFCC-174 | SEO & Analytics & AB Testing | BA: 0.5 days  FED: 3 days  Testing: 3 days | TBC |  *(blank)* | **Outstanding - what tool is doing this AI extraction?**  @Emma Kirwan to check with Miranda  Needs to be for PLP (exists today), but if beyond PLP or something else, then we need to confirm |

**SFCC-173**
> | SFCC-173 | SEO & Analytics & AB Testing | BA: 0.5 days  FED: 3 days Testing: 3 days | TBC |  *(blank)* | Contentful dependency  @Emma Kirwan / @Rebecca Jourdan to check with Miranda |

**SFCC-724**
> | SFCC-724 | SEO & Analytics & AB Testing | BA - 2 days  FED - 5 days  BED - @Victor T. Crisostomo  Testing - @Krizel B. Bartolome @Joseph Molina | Approved pending prioritisation |  *(blank)* | @Dani Rivett 's commentary on the ticket: " The content team are really keen to be able to have this feature to execute numerous SEO requests and to build long-term page rankings for popular searches." |

Note (my observation): **none of the three carries a BED/DEV number.** SFCC-173 and SFCC-174 have no BED line at all; SFCC-724's BED and Testing cells hold *names instead of numbers* — i.e. unestimated, assigned to Victor Crisostomo (BED) and Krizel Bartolome / Joseph Molina (Testing).

### 1b. The capacity table — verbatim

Preceding narrative, quoted exactly:
> **Enhancement Capacity**
>
> We have 2 sprints of Enhancements capacity, equivalent to 20 business days. With four disciplines involved — 1 x BA, 1 x FED, 1 x BED, and 1 x Testing — this gives us a combined total of 80 business days.
>
> To date the following amount has been approved by Zimmermann team and consumed:

| *(blank)* | **BA** | **FED** | **DEV** | **QA** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SFCC-155 | 0.5 days | 1 day | 1 day | 2 days |
| SFCC-143 | 0.5 days | 2 days | 2 days | 2 days |
| SFCC-142 | 1 day | 3.5 days | 3.5 days | 2 days |
| SFCC-133 | 0.5 days | 3 days | 3 days | 3 days |
| **SFCC-173** | **0.5 days** | **3 days** | **N/A** | **3 days** |
| **Total Consumed as of** | 3 days | 12.5 days | 9.5 days | 12 days |
| **Total Remaining** | 17 days | 7.5 days | 10.5 days | 8 days |

(The header cell reads literally "**Total Consumed as of**" with nothing after "of" — an unrendered date macro or an unfinished sentence. There is no as-at date on the totals.)

### 1c. VERDICT ON THE CLAIM: **TRUE**

SFCC-173's FED 3 days is a line item in the consumed table and is arithmetically inside the 12.5-day FED total, while the same ticket's Status in the enhancements table above is `TBC`.

Proof by arithmetic on the quoted figures:

| | BA | FED | DEV | QA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sum of the 5 listed rows | 0.5+0.5+1+0.5+0.5 = **3** | 1+2+3.5+3+3 = **12.5** | 1+2+3.5+3+N/A = **9.5** | 2+2+2+3+3 = **12** |
| Page's stated total | 3 | 12.5 | 9.5 | 12 |
| **Match?** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

Every column reconciles exactly *including* the SFCC-173 row. Strip SFCC-173 out and FED consumed becomes **9.5 days**, remaining **10.5 days** — not the 12.5 / 7.5 the page states. So the 3 FED days are unambiguously counted.

**The inconsistency is sharper than the claim suggests.** The consumed table is not driven by the Status column in either direction:

- **One `TBC` row is counted:** SFCC-173.

## Avalara is stated four ways, and Confluence still formally asks

I said three. It's four, and page 470843399 asks the question outright: *"What is the confirmed, agreed scope for Avalara? Which storefronts are in, and which are not?"*

| Source | Date | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| PRC-07, signed off Emma/Rebecca | 24 Jun | AU, EU, US, **UK** |
| architecture.md | 19 Jun | US, NZ, New Caledonia, EU domestic; UK native |
| PAY-067 | Jul extract | US, NZ, New Caledonia only |
| **SFCC-875 + vendor meeting + site.xml cartridge audit** | ~4 Sep | **All four domestic sites** |

The two newest and most concrete both say all four domestic — which is exactly what SFCC-946 proposes to expand into. One page contradicts itself inside a single table: *"confirmed — no Avalara for EU Domestic"* sits next to Emma's own answer *"UK does use Avalara."*

## One correction to my own verdict

I called SFCC-946's FE work near-zero because the payload renders identically whichever engine computed it. That holds, but I was too clean about it. The line-item label logic **reads Avalara's own `tax_type` field** (`Output` = tax, `LandedCost` = duty), so an engine change isn't automatically inert. For EU/UK domestic it renders a single tax line either way so it very likely is — but that should be confirmed, not assumed.

More useful: there **is** a substantial body of real FE tax work, and it's genuinely unestimated anywhere. Per-storefront gross/net display (US Domestic is the only storefront where displayed price ≠ price paid), per-storefront subtotal labels, `DUTIES`/`TAXES` vs `DUTIES EXCLUDED` line logic, a Contentful-sourced DDP/DDU disclaimer, and a "Hidden DDP" duties message on **PDP** for Global-e markets. That lives under SFCC-462 and SFCC-43 — so 2 days here double-books it, and the real total is well above 2 wherever it lands.

## Co-browsing is decisively unsizeable

Not just under-sized. CQL across the whole space returns **zero pages** for co-browsing in any spelling. No vendor statement from InsideChat or anyone. The Client Services persona page — the persona that owns the epic — never mentions Inside Chat at all. The row has no BED figure and no status. The only FE obligations on record are "it's a pop-up, visibility is the vendor's call" and "don't initialise before Didomi consent".

## One blocker to add to your list

Avalara **sandbox credentials are blank**, recorded "confirmed 04 Sep 2026", marked CRITICAL. That blocks all Avalara testing — not just this row.

**What you're missing:** I've now put twelve decisions in front of you and the honest risk is that the list itself becomes the reason nothing moves. If you only act on one thing from this audit, make it the capacity conversation — the −10 day FED hole is true at the tracker's own numbers, before any of my corrections, and it's the only finding that doesn't depend on someone else answering a question first. Everything else on the list is a question for Tash, Emma, Victor or a vendor, and those can run in parallel once the capacity reality is on the table. ## How much of SFCC-724 is already covered? — my read

**SFCC-724's own description**, quoted:
> "As a Site Merchandiser, I want to flag specific filter combinations (e.g. Dresses + White) as indexable pages with their own clean URL and metadata, so that Zimmermann can rank for high-value search terms like "white dresses" without having to create and maintain a separate category for each one.
>
> Currently, all filtered PLP URLs canonicalise back to the base category page per DMU-023, meaning Google does not index them as standalone pages. This enhancement would allow a merchandiser to opt specific filter combinations into indexability via Business Manager, and set a unique title tag, meta description, and SEO paragraph per combination. The PWA Kit would then render the correct metadata for those URLs.
>
> Note: the SEO agency (Sparro / Tell No Lies) must define the URL structure rules and metadata templates before build can begin. This is a custom build — effort estimate required before prioritisation."

Labels: `DMU-023` only — **the same requirement ID as SFCC-562/563.**

### Verdict: roughly **one of five** component parts is genuinely covered. The half the ticket is named after is not.

| SFCC-724 component | Covered? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1. BM opt-in to indexability per filter combo | **YES — real overlap** | SFCC-562 AC 6 |
| 2. Canonical behaviour for opted-in combos | **YES — real overlap** | SFCC-562 AC 5 |
| 3. Clean URL for the filter combination | **NO** | Undefined everywhere |
| 4. Per-filter title tag | **NO** | SFCC-568 is category-object-bound |
| 5. Per-filter meta description | **NO** | SFCC-569 is category-object-bound |
| 6. Per-filter SEO paragraph | **ADJACENT, not equivalent** | SFCC-577, storefront-level, 0 ACs |

**The two AC lines that genuinely overlap**, quoted from SFCC-562:

> "Facet combinations Tell No Lies/Sparro confirm as having real standalone search demand (see SFCC-571 dependency) are excluded from that rule and get a self-referencing canonical instead, per SFCC-571's per-facet-type split - never both a robots.txt block and a canonical on the same URL."

> "Business Manager gives a Site Merchandiser a way to override the canonical target on a specific indexable filter URL - exact BM mechanism TBC, see Assumptions."

Between them these cover *"allow a merchandiser to opt specific filter combinations into indexability via Business Manager"* — genuinely the same capability. If SFCC-724 is estimated as if that were greenfield, it is double-counted against SFCC-562.

**What is NOT covered — and I checked this against the actual implementation source, not just the titles.** SFCC-724's *"set a unique title tag, meta description, and SEO paragraph per combination"* has no home:

- **SFCC-568** (Title Tag Generation) AC 1, quoted: *"PDP and PLP/category page title tags render from product.pageTitle / category.pageTitle (already implemented) - confirm this already satisfies the requirement for those two templates with no further PWA code work."*
- **SFCC-569** (Meta Description) AC 1, quoted: *"PDP and PLP/category meta description already render from product.pageDescription / category.pageDescription (and pageMetaTags where set) - confirm this already satisfies the requirement for those two templates."*

Both source metadata from the **SFCC category object**. A facet combination is not a category — that is the entire premise of SFCC-724 (*"without having to create and maintain a separate category for each one"*). So there is structurally nowhere for per-filter metadata to live under the current design. **This is net-new build, and it is the larger half of the ticket.**

- **SFCC-577** covers the SEO copy field at *"all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level"* — per-storefront-per-category, not per-filter-combination. With zero ACs, its boundary is undefined; it cannot be relied on as covering the per-filter case without someone writing that AC.

### Three risks I'd raise before this estimate is signed off

1. **`SFCC-571`'s "per-facet-type split" does not exist.** SFCC-562 AC 5 defers to it explicitly. SFCC-571's actual ACs say only: *"Filtered/faceted PLP query parameters are disallowed via a parameter-pattern rule - exact pattern TBC, see Assumptions."* **Dangling cross-reference.** The indexable-facet allow-list that both SFCC-562 and SFCC-724 depend on is not written down in either story, or anywhere in Confluence. Both are blocked on the same undelivered Tell No Lies/Sparro input.

2. **SFCC-724 and SFCC-562 both carry label `DMU-023`, and they specify opposite behaviours** — 562 suppresses filtered PLPs, 724 promotes selected ones. They are the rule and its exception filed as independent tickets against one requirement ID. Per your own duplicate-detection heuristic (shared DMU-/SPR- labels), this is exactly the shape that needs reconciling before either is estimated.

3. **SFCC-573 AC 4 will conflict with SFCC-724 if 724 ships.** Quoted: *"Filtered/faceted PLP variants that SFCC-562 canonicalizes to the base PLP do NOT get their own ItemList/CollectionPage describing the filtered subset."* An indexable, self-canonical filter page under SFCC-724 falls outside that carve-out and **would need its own ItemList/CollectionPage** describing the filtered subset — unscoped work in SFCC-573, not counted in either estimate.

content.text: This one corrects something I told you twice. Let me fix the report first.

input.old_string: **SFCC-174 duplicates SFCC-572**, which sits in epic SFCC-22 with **7 real acceptance criteria**. More broadly there are **two parallel SEO backlogs**: SFCC-724 ≈ SFCC-563 + SFCC-577, and SFCC-563 carries the *same* `DMU-023` label. Sizing the Enhancements copies books the same days twice. Deciding that the Enhancements epic owns no SEO work would recover ~6 FED days — most of the gap.
input.new_string:
**SFCC-174 duplicates SFCC-572**, which sits in epic SFCC-22 with **7 real acceptance criteria**. That one holds.

**Correction — the SFCC-724 duplication is much weaker than first reported.** An earlier draft of this audit said SFCC-724 ≈ SFCC-563 + SFCC-577 and that moving SEO off the tracker would recover ~6 FED days. Both statements were wrong:

- **SFCC-563 is a dead shell.** Merged into SFCC-562 on 2026-09-14; its description says *"do not groom this story separately"*; **AC count 0**. The real comparison is SFCC-562 + SFCC-577.
- **SFCC-577 has zero ACs** and is scoped *"at individual storefront level"* on category/PLP pages — not per filter combination. Its boundary is undefined, so it can't be relied on as covering anything specific.
- **Only 2 of SFCC-724's 6 components are genuinely covered.** SFCC-562's AC5 (self-canonical for facet combos with real search demand) and AC6 (BM override of canonical target on an indexable filter URL) do cover the merchandiser opt-in. **The per-filter clean URL, title tag and meta description have no home anywhere** — SFCC-568 and SFCC-569 both source metadata from the **SFCC category object**, and a facet combination is not a category. That is the entire premise of SFCC-724, and it is the larger half.

So the recoverable duplication is roughly **SFCC-174's 3 days plus perhaps 1.5 of SFCC-724's 5 — about 4.5 FED days, not 6.** Still worth having; not "most of the gap".

**Three further risks on SFCC-724 that no estimate reflects:**

1. **SFCC-562 AC5 defers to a "per-facet-type split" in SFCC-571 that does not exist.** SFCC-571's actual ACs say only *"exact pattern TBC"*. The indexable-facet allow-list both stories depend on is written down nowhere, in Jira or Confluence.
2. **SFCC-724 and SFCC-562 carry the same `DMU-023` label and specify opposite behaviours** — 562 suppresses filtered PLPs, 724 promotes selected ones. They are a rule and its exception filed as independent tickets against one requirement ID.
3. **SFCC-573 AC4 would conflict if SFCC-724 ships.** It states filtered variants canonicalised to base do *not* get their own ItemList/CollectionPage. An indexable self-canonical filter page falls outside that carve-out and would need one — unscoped in both estimates.

**And FAQ/Article schema has no requirement behind it at all.** The specified JSON-LD set is DMU-038 (Product, PDP), DMU-039 (CollectionPage/BreadcrumbList/ItemList, PLP), DMU-040 (LocalBusiness), DMU-041 (Organisation), DMU-042. **No FAQ, Article, HowTo or QAPage requirement exists anywhere.** So SFCC-173 is genuinely net-new scope, not a variant of SFCC-572/573 — which supports the UNDER verdict rather than a duplication one.

Two late agents corrected me on things I'd already told you. Both matter.

## Correction 1 — the SEO duplication was overstated

I said "SFCC-724 ≈ SFCC-563 + SFCC-577" and that moving SEO off the tracker recovers **~6 FED days, most of the gap**. Both wrong.

- **SFCC-563 is a dead shell** — merged into SFCC-562 on 14 September, its description says *"do not groom this story separately"*, **zero ACs**.
- **SFCC-577 has zero ACs** and is scoped *"at individual storefront level"* on category pages, not per filter combination.
- **Only 2 of SFCC-724's 6 components are genuinely covered** — SFCC-562's AC5 and AC6 cover the merchandiser opt-in and the canonical override. The **per-filter clean URL, title tag and meta description have no home anywhere**, because SFCC-568 and SFCC-569 both source metadata from the **SFCC category object**, and a facet combination isn't a category. That's the entire premise of SFCC-724, and it's the larger half.

Recoverable duplication is about **4.5 FED days, not 6**. Still worth having, but not most of the gap.

Three risks that came with it: SFCC-562's AC5 defers to a "per-facet-type split" in SFCC-571 **that doesn't exist**; SFCC-724 and SFCC-562 carry the same `DMU-023` label while specifying **opposite** behaviours; and SFCC-573's AC4 would conflict if 724 ships.

Also worth knowing: **FAQ/Article schema has no DMU requirement at all.** The specified set is DMU-038 through 042 — Product, CollectionPage, LocalBusiness, Organisation. No FAQ, Article, HowTo or QAPage anywhere. So SFCC-173 is genuinely net-new, which supports the UNDER verdict rather than a duplication one.

## Correction 2 — the co-browsing vendor answer exists, unread

Last turn I told you there was "no vendor statement from InsideChat or anyone". That was based on a text search, and it missed an **attachment**.

Page 264765445 carries **`Manual - INSIDE - Co-Browse.pdf`, 4.0 MB** — a dedicated Powerfront product manual, supplied by Zimmermann as an official technical file. The page's Inside Chat row literally reads *"Co-browse:"* with the manual beneath it.

SFCC-858's headline note is *"Is this functionality available today? **Assuming** InsideChat has this functionality."* The document answering that has been sitting in Confluence the whole time. **That's the cheapest action in this entire audit.** It won't remove the two real FE costs — the consent prompt and PII/payment masking — but it collapses the main unknown.

Two more on that row: SFCC-858 needs a **second consent surface** (an in-session prompt before an agent may co-browse, *"wording and design TBC"*) that appears in **no consent document**, including the one meant for Legal sign-off. And Inside Chat's load mechanism is contradicted **five ways including inside the TSD itself** — §4.1 says the token is "Likely NOT PWA-owned", §7.2 says "**Not a GTM tag**". That decides whether FED owns the story at all.

---

Updated document above. Both corrections are marked in place rather than quietly patched.

**What you're missing:** the pattern in both corrections is the same, and it's worth more than either one. My first pass concluded "duplicate" and "no vendor answer" from things that looked settled — a ticket title, a text search. Both fell over on a second look. The tracker has the same failure mode at scale: **"Approved" was read off a status column, and estimates were read off ticket titles**, and nearly every one that got a second look moved. Before you take the −10 day number to Tash, be ready for someone to ask whether the audit itself holds — it does on the capacity arithmetic, which is verified twice against v17 and doesn't depend on any judgement call. The per-ticket verdicts are good but they are my reconstruction, not a negotiated re-estimate, and two of them already moved under scrutiny today. Lead with the arithmetic.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab to test responsive layouts. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

# 14 — Inside Chat (Customer Service Chat)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Inside Chat (by Powerfront) is the customer-service live chat widget on Zimmermann storefronts.

Per HPC-039/040, the widget is a **direct PWA head tag** — not loaded via GTM. In the previous Magento implementation Tryzens hardcoded the script in the page head. The PWA is to follow the same pattern. Vicky@Zimmermann confirmed this approach as best practice (2026-07-02).

The PWA loads the Inside Chat script asynchronously, post-Didomi-consent, so it never blocks first paint. The site token (`INSIDE_CHAT_SITE_TOKEN`) is a public identifier held as an MRT environment variable and embedded in the script tag at load time.

Page visibility rules and widget configuration are owned by Zimmermann / Inside Chat / Tryzens — outside PWA scope.

## 2. PWA implementation summary

| Concern        | Detail                                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Load mechanism | Direct PWA head tag — async script inject post-Didomi-consent |
| Env var        | `INSIDE_CHAT_SITE_TOKEN` (public; safe in bundle)             |
| Consent gate   | Didomi — consent category TBC (Zimmermann Privacy to confirm) |
| Scope          | All storefronts                                               |
| LCP impact     | None — async, post-consent, never on critical path            |

## 3. Open items

1. **The script tag / site token.** From Zimmermann / Inside Chat / Tryzens (the equivalent of what Tryzens hardcoded in Magento)
2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann to confirm the Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.
