# 13 — Google Tag Manager on Addingwell (Data Layer, Consent Mode v2, Tag Orchestration)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Google Tag Manager (GTM) is the tag orchestration layer for analytics and marketing on Zimmermann storefronts. The GTM container is **hosted on Addingwell** — a Didomi-owned managed tagging server — so the browser fetches `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain (`ruffles.zimmermann.com`), not `www.googletagmanager.com`. The tags deployed via GTM (GA4, Meta Pixel, and any other tags Tell No Lies configures) are therefore served through Addingwell.

> **Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM** (confirmed 2026-06-09). They load as separate **frontend-direct** tags, Didomi-consent-gated, not housed in the GTM container or served via Addingwell.

The storefront's responsibility ends at correctly emitting a comprehensive data layer and pointing the loader at the Addingwell tagging-server URL. All downstream tags are loaded, configured, and maintained inside the GTM container by Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner Tell No Lies, who also operates the Addingwell workspace.

In scope at the PWA layer:

- GTM container loader (`gtm.js`) injection from the Addingwell first-party domain, post-Didomi consent
- A native, SFCC-aligned data layer (`window.dataLayer`) populated on every relevant event
- Google Consent Mode v2 default and update signal emission, propagated from Didomi to GTM
- Enhanced Conversions data — a hashed email at order confirmation (REG-056)

Out of scope of this document (owned by Tell No Lies):

- All tag configuration inside GTM (which tags fire, with what data, on which triggers)
- Downstream vendor scripts loaded via GTM: GA4, Meta Pixel, etc.
- Tag-side consent gating beyond what Consent Mode v2 conveys
- Experiment definitions in Optimizely; heatmap configuration in Crazy Egg (and the loading of those two scripts, which are frontend-direct tags owned by Tell No Lies — not GTM tags, per the note in §1)

The handover boundary is fixed by AAB-001 and AAB-002: Accenture emits the data layer; Tell No Lies consumes it inside GTM.

### Responsibilities boundary — Didomi, PWA, Addingwell, GTM, Tell No Lies

| Party | Role | PWA relationship |
|---|---|---|
| **Didomi** (CMP) | Shows the cookie banner, captures consent, and signals which purposes/vendors are allowed. | PWA integrates the `@didomi/react` SDK and gates scripts on its signals. |
| **PWA** (storefront) | (1) Always emits the first-party data layer; (2) after Didomi grants consent, loads the GTM container from the Addingwell URL; (3) emits Consent Mode v2 signals derived from Didomi's state. | This is the full PWA scope. |
| **Addingwell** (Didomi-owned) | First-party hosting for the GTM container — serves `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann subdomain instead of `googletagmanager.com`. | PWA points the loader at the Addingwell URL; nothing more. |
| **GTM container** | Holds and fires GA4, Meta, and other TNL-configured tags. (Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM — they are frontend-direct tags; see §1 note.) | Out of PWA scope. |
| **Tell No Lies** | Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner; configures the GTM container and operates the Addingwell workspace. | Owns everything downstream of the data layer. |

In one line: Didomi = consent; PWA = data layer + Consent Mode + load-GTM-post-consent; Addingwell = first-party hosting for GTM; GTM = the tag container; Tell No Lies = configures it all.

## 2. Vendor relationship

- **Vendor (orchestration layer):** Google — Google Tag Manager.
- **Vendor (hosting):** Addingwell, a Didomi-owned managed server-side GTM platform. The GTM container is hosted on Addingwell; the browser loads it from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain. Container IDs and Addingwell tagging-server URLs are provided to the PWA team by Tell No Lies.
- **Container ID (likely single).** Tell No Lies expects a **single GTM container ID** across all environments (to be confirmed — 2026-06-09 call). Any environment separation would be handled via the data layer rather than separate container IDs.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
Page load
        │
        ▼
Didomi loads first (strictly necessary) and emits Consent Mode v2 defaults to gtag
        gtag('consent', 'default', { ad_storage: 'denied', analytics_storage: 'denied', … })
        │
        ▼
Data layer is populated with first-party SFCC events regardless of consent (AAB-003)
        window.dataLayer.push({ event: 'page_view', page: { … } })
        │
        ▼
Didomi resolves the user's consent choice
        gtag('consent', 'update', { ad_storage: 'granted', analytics_storage: 'granted', … })
        │
        ▼
GTM container loads from the Addingwell first-party subdomain
(`https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/9i683nqysc4y77v.js?awl=M8PJ5D`), when analytics or
marketing consent is granted
        │
        ▼
Tell No Lies-configured tags fire per consent state — GA4 collects (with consent),
marketing tags only on grant. All tag requests route through Addingwell.
```

- The data layer is always populated (AAB-003). It is first-party SFCC state — not a third-party script — and never gates on consent.
- The GTM container script is served from the Addingwell first-party subdomain and is loaded only after Didomi grants the relevant purpose. Because the request is first-party, it survives most cookie/tracking-prevention browser modes.
- Consent Mode v2 defaults are emitted as soon as Didomi reports user state, even before the GTM container loads. This follows Google's recommended pattern and enables Google's cookieless modelling downstream (configured by Tell No Lies).

## 4. Authentication and credentials

- GTM container ID: **`GTM-M8PJ5D`** — confirmed by Zimmermann 2026-06-10. Public; embedded in the loader.
- Addingwell tagging-server URL (`GTM_SERVER_URL`) — public, embedded in the loader. The first-party subdomain is **`ruffles.zimmermann.com`** (confirmed 2026-06-09). It is a Zimmermann-owned subdomain resolving to Addingwell infrastructure (DNS CNAME owned by Zimmermann; TLS cert managed by Addingwell). Per-environment host provisioning is a Zimmermann/Tell No Lies/Addingwell task.
- No secret credentials at the storefront layer. The Addingwell workspace API credentials live inside Tell No Lies' Addingwell account, not the PWA bundle.

### Loader snippets (Tell No Lies, 2026-07-01)

Confirmed Addingwell loader snippets provided by Tell No Lies on 2026-07-01. These supersede the vanilla GTM snippet Zimmermann sent on 2026-06-10. The Addingwell loader uses a custom path (`/9i683nqysc4y77v.js`) and `awl=` query parameter (the container ID with the `GTM-` prefix stripped), not the standard GTM CDN URL.

In `<head>` as high as possible, post-Didomi-consent:
```html
<!-- Google Tag Manager -->
<script>(function(w,d,s,l,i){w[l]=w[l]||[];w[l].push({'gtm.start':
new Date().getTime(),event:'gtm.js'});var f=d.getElementsByTagName(s)[0],
j=d.createElement(s),dl=l!='dataLayer'?'&l='+l:'';j.async=true;j.src=
'https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/9i683nqysc4y77v.js?awl='+i.replace(/^GTM-/, '')+dl;f.parentNode.insertBefore(j,f);
})(window,document,'script','dataLayer','GTM-M8PJ5D');</script>
<!-- End Google Tag Manager -->
```

Immediately after `<body>` (noscript fallback):
```html
<!-- Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
<noscript><iframe src="https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/ns.html?id=GTM-M8PJ5D"
height="0" width="0" style="display:none;visibility:hidden"></iframe></noscript>
<!-- End Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
```

> **Note:** The noscript fallback renders when JavaScript is disabled. Because Didomi also requires JS, when this iframe fires the consent signal is irrelevant; the noscript path is a graceful degradation row.

## 5. Data layer schema

Per AAB-002, the data layer is the single source of truth. The storefront emits structured events for the lifecycle moments below. Event names follow GA4 e-commerce conventions for compatibility with the most common downstream consumer.

> **Unconfirmed — pending Tell No Lies sign-off (open item 3).** The schema below is a proposal based on GA4 conventions and PRD requirements (AAB-002, AAB-004, AAB-005). Tell No Lies must confirm it satisfies the GTM tags before implementation.

| Event | When | Key fields |
|---|---|---|
| `page_view` | Every page load and SPA route change | page type, storefront, locale, customer hash (if logged in), authenticated state, customer group |
| `view_item_list` | PLP or search results page | list ID, list name, items[] |
| `view_item` | PDP load | item (id, name, brand, category, price, currency, variant, size) |
| `select_item` | PLP tile click | list context, item |
| `add_to_cart` | Add-to-bag success | item, currency, value |
| `remove_from_cart` | Cart remove | item, currency, value |
| `view_cart` | Cart page load | items[], currency, value |
| `begin_checkout` | Checkout entry | items[], currency, value |
| `add_shipping_info` | Delivery method selected | shipping_tier, items[], currency, value |
| `add_payment_info` | Payment method selected | payment_type, items[], currency, value |
| `purchase` | Order placed | transaction_id, value, currency, tax, shipping, items[], hashed email (REG-056) |
| `refund` | Order refunded (where surfaced in storefront) | transaction_id, value |
| `login` | Successful login | method |
| `sign_up` | Successful registration | method |
| `consent_decision` | Didomi banner dismissed | decision_summary (non-PII) |

Attributes available on every event (AAB-004 Optimizely segmentation; AAB-005 Crazy Egg):

- `storefront_region` (AU, US, UK, EU, EU-INTL, HK, ME) — sourced from Zimmermann's geolocation logic and the Global-e platform (AAB-002)
- `locale` (en-AU, fr-EU, …)
- `currency` (storefront base currency)
- `authenticated` (boolean)
- `customer_group` (SFCC customer group)
- `loyalty_status` (Retail Rewards tier)
- `visitor_type` (new vs returning)
- `existing_customer` (boolean — returning vs first-time customer, AAB-002)
- `lifetime_value` (customer lifetime value, AAB-002)
- `device_type` (mobile, tablet, desktop)

## 6. Consent Mode v2 mapping (Didomi → gtag)

> **Left column unconfirmed.** The Didomi purpose names below are Didomi's standard IAB TCF identifiers. Zimmermann's actual Didomi configuration may use different IDs — verify against the provisioned account once Didomi open item 1 is resolved. The right column (Consent Mode v2 signals) is from Google's official Consent Mode v2 documentation and is authoritative.

| Didomi purpose | Consent Mode v2 signal |
|---|---|
| `measure_audience` / `analytics` | `analytics_storage` |
| `select_personalized_ads` / `targeted_advertising` | `ad_storage`, `ad_personalization`, `ad_user_data` |
| `personalize_content` | `personalization_storage` |
| `functional` | `functionality_storage`, `security_storage` |

Defaults emitted before Didomi resolves are all denied (fail-closed). The update is emitted as soon as Didomi reports the user's choice. The `region` parameter on the default `gtag('consent', 'default', …)` call is used where regulation differs (e.g. `region: ['US']` for the US opt-out posture; rest of world is opt-in). The per-region default states themselves are owned by the Didomi configuration.

## 7. Performance and loading strategy

- The GTM loader script is small and loaded asynchronously, deferred until after Didomi grants the relevant consent. It does not contribute to LCP.
- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Addingwell first-party hostname (`GTM_SERVER_URL`) is emitted from the document head once consent is granted. No preconnect to `www.googletagmanager.com` is needed — the container is not served from there.

## 8. Multi-region behaviour

- One GTM container ID across all storefronts (and most likely across all environments too — Tell No Lies to confirm), with region and storefront discrimination via the data layer attributes in §5. This is the assumed Tell No Lies pattern and the simplest model to maintain.
- Per-region Consent Mode default states (US opt-out posture vs rest-of-world opt-in posture) are emitted via the `region` parameter on the default `gtag('consent', 'default', …)` call. The actual per-region defaults are configured in the Didomi Console; the storefront translates Didomi state into Consent Mode signals without holding regional logic itself.

## 9. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| GTM container fails to load | Storefront unaffected. The data layer continues to populate; tags simply do not fire. |
| Didomi never resolves consent | GTM is never loaded; Consent Mode defaults remain denied. Pages work; analytics is absent. |
| A downstream tag configured by Tell No Lies errors | Tag-level — does not affect the page. GTM isolates tag failures. |
| A data-layer push throws | Every `dataLayer.push` is wrapped in `try / catch`; on failure the storefront logs to monitoring but never blocks the user flow. |

## 10. Security and privacy

- The hashed email on `purchase` is a SHA-256 hash of the normalised customer email (REG-056). No raw email appears in the data layer. Normalisation follows Google's Enhanced Conversions spec: trim whitespace, lowercase; for `@gmail.com` / `@googlemail.com` addresses additionally remove dots from the local part and strip any `+suffix`.
- No PII appears in any data layer event beyond the hashed email. Customer IDs are hashed when present.
- No card data ever reaches the data layer. PCI scope is not affected by this integration.

## 11. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **Addingwell tagging-server URL (per environment).** The production first-party subdomain is confirmed as `ruffles.zimmermann.com` (2026-06-09). **Zimmermann/Accenture** to provision the equivalent first-party host for each non-production environment (each must be first-party to that environment's storefront domain). The PWA points the loader at this URL.
2. **Data layer schema confirmation.** GTM's own tags (GA4, Meta) consume the data layer. The **frontend-direct** Optimizely and Crazy Egg scripts (which are *not* GTM tags — see §1) may also read it, but whether they require any PWA-emitted attributes at all is open (AAB-004 / AAB-005 — Tell No Lies to confirm; may be dropped). Tell No Lies to confirm the event and attribute schema in §5 satisfies the GTM tags, and to confirm whether any additional attributes are needed for Optimizely segmentation (AAB-004) or Crazy Egg filtering (AAB-005).

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: ShareOnboardingGuide
tools.description:
Upload the ONBOARDING.md in the current directory and return a share link teammates can open in Claude Code. Call this after the user has confirmed the final content.

When called with the default mode='check': if a local ONBOARDING.md is present, uploads it to the most-recently-updated org guide (or creates one if none exist) and returns a fresh link. If no local file is present, returns the existing link without uploading (status: has_existing).

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_resize
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab to test responsive layouts. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

content.text:
Both of these turn out to have real technical merit behind the pushback — not just "client wants a smaller number." I can't hit Jira or Confluence right now (it's down on my side too), so this is built from the research already gathered in this session plus two repo docs I just re-read in full. Here's the sense check.

## SFCC-857 — Emarsys Web Extend: the client has a point, with one condition

[13-gtm.md](.docs/integration/13-gtm.md) settles this more than I'd realised last night. The AAB-002 data layer spec (§5) already defines `add_to_cart`, `view_cart`, `view_item`, `purchase` (with `transaction_id`, `value`, `items[]`, hashed email) and `login` — that's every field Web Extend needs for cart abandonment, browse abandonment and revenue tracking. And the architecture doc I found yesterday independently calls all of Emarsys "no PWA involvement, out-of-band."

Put those together and the likely delivery model is: Tell No Lies writes a GTM Custom HTML tag that translates the *existing* data layer pushes into Web Extend's `ScarabQueue.push()` calls — exactly the pattern already used for GA4 and Meta on this project. If that's the plan, FED's job is done the moment AAB-002 ships (Sprint 7, separately budgeted), and this ticket really does carry close to zero incremental cost. That's the client's position, and the evidence supports it.

**Recommend: 0.5–1 day**, down from 3 — conditional on Web Extend being GTM-tag-configured against the data layer rather than needing its own on-page SDK calls. If TNL can't do it that way, it's closer to **4 days**, not the original 3 or my earlier 6 — lower than my number last night because the loader and consent-gating cost is shared infrastructure under SFCC-107, not specific to this ticket.

## SFCC-858 — Co-browsing: this confirms something I'd flagged but not read

Last night I found an unopened Powerfront manual, `Manual - INSIDE - Co-Browse.pdf`, sitting in Confluence, and said reading it was the cheapest unblock in the whole audit. Natasha's "confirmed this will be done via InsideChat" is that answer arriving without anyone needing to open the PDF: co-browsing is a native Powerfront capability, not something built from scratch.

That collapses the session mechanics to zero. What's left is genuinely still open, not resolved by this message: the ticket's own AC says the consent prompt wording and design are "TBC" — that's a real design question whether or not the underlying engine is vendor-owned, and PII/payment masking during a session still needs confirming as vendor-config rather than app code.

**Recommend: 0–1 day**, down from 3 — 0 if Zimmermann accepts InsideChat's own native consent and masking UI, ~1 if they want a Zimmermann-branded modal wrapping the vendor's trigger (still small, because the actual co-browse engine stays vendor-owned).

---

## Draft reply to Natasha

> Hey Tash! Good sense checks, both hold up.
>
> **SFCC-857 (Emarsys):** agree, FED should come down a lot. The data layer we're already building for GA4/Meta (AAB-002) already carries everything Web Extend needs, view/cart/purchase/identity. If Tell No Lies configures Web Extend as a GTM tag reading that data layer, same as GA4, there's genuinely no separate front-end build. FED down to 0.5-1 day. One thing to confirm with TNL: is that actually how they'll wire it, or does Web Extend need its own calls in the app code? If it's the second one it's closer to 4 days, but I don't think that's the likely path here.
>
> **SFCC-858 (co-browsing):** great, that answers the open question on the ticket. If InSide is handling the co-browse session itself, FED drops to 0-1 day. The only thing left for us is whether Zimmermann wants their own branded consent prompt before a session starts, or is happy with InSide's default one. If it's InSide's own, it's 0. If we want it branded, call it 1 day for a small wrapper, the session itself still isn't something we're building.
>
> Can get these onto the tracker today, just say if you want them as Jira comments or I update the Confluence row directly.

Wording's yours to adjust. Since Atlassian's down on my end I can't post either the Jira comments or the Confluence row edit right now — say the word once it's back and I'll do it, or you can paste the above straight into your reply.

I've updated the audit memory with both revisions so a future session doesn't quote my original 6-day and 4.5-day figures as final.

Full write-up produced as a standalone document, not stored here.

(SFCC-135, 704, 724, 859, 946) are 17.5 days against that 7.5 — a **10-day hole**. BA finishes
~11 days spare: the capacity model treats four disciplines as interchangeable and the work mix
is FED-heavy.

estimates a paragraph. None is in any sprint.

- **SFCC-946** (Avalara) — PRC-07, signed off 24 June by Emma/Rebecca, already puts AU/EU/US/UK
  in the baseline this "expansion" targets. Conflicts with PAY-067 and architecture.md. FE is
  payload-driven (`order-summary` not overridden, renders `basket.taxTotal`), so ~0.5 day.

  deliverable is inside Global-E's iframe; zero affected customers per its own note.

  SFCC-724 ≈ SFCC-563 + SFCC-577. Moving SEO off this tracker recovers ~6 FED days.
- **SFCC-156** is linked `Blocks`, **not** Duplicate, to SFCC-135 — High, 7 ACs, 3 front-end.
- **SFCC-710** is a *reversal* of SFCC-434, which `product-detail/index.tsx:590` records Jasmijn
  as having confirmed ("PDP badge has no confirmation message").

**Two live defects found in passing:** the `/social-callback` route gap
([[project-routes-static-export-trap]]), and SFCC-947 — a real WCAG 2.2 AA duplicate-CTA defect

approved-in-principle, so the capacity table treats unspecified and contradicted work as booked
cost.

whether Enhancements owns any SEO, and the Avalara baseline. Related:
